items.title: [Bug]: Local Ollama context resolved from GGUF max instead of Modelfile num_ctx — step 2b preempts the local-aware steps

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

For **local** Ollama endpoints, `get_model_context_length()` reports the GGUF training maximum instead of the effective `num_ctx` baked into the model's Modelfile. Two functions read the same `/api/show` response with **opposite field priority**, and the one that prefers the GGUF value runs first.

The over-reported value is also written to the persistent cache, so it survives restarts.

## Root cause

Three call sites resolve context from `/api/show`:

| Function | Step in `get_model_context_length()` | Reads first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_query_ollama_api_show` | **2b** | `model_info.*.context_length` (GGUF training max) |
| `_query_local_context_length` | 3 | `parameters` → `num_ctx` |
| `query_ollama_num_ctx` | 5e | `parameters` → `num_ctx` |

`_query_ollama_api_show` documents the flip deliberately:

> For hosted servers the GGUF `model_info.*.context_length` is the authoritative source: the user can't set their own `num_ctx`, and the OpenAI-compat `/v1/models` endpoint correctly omits `context_length` […] The order is flipped vs `query_ollama_num_ctx()` because local users control `num_ctx` themselves; hosted users can't.

The reasoning is sound, but step 2b has **no local/hosted discrimination** — it fires for `127.0.0.1` too, and it returns before steps 3 and 5e, which implement the intended local behaviour. So the local path never runs.

Step 2b then persists its result via `save_context_length()`, poisoning `context_length_cache.yaml`. Clearing the cache does not help: the next resolution re-derives the same wrong value.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. A model whose Modelfile num_ctx is BELOW its native context
printf 'FROM qwen3.6:27b\nPARAMETER num_ctx 131072\n' > Modelfile
ollama create qwen3.6:27b-128k -f Modelfile

# 2. Ollama allocates 131072 — confirmed
ollama ps
# NAME              SIZE   PROCESSOR  CONTEXT
# qwen3.6:27b-128k  21 GB  100% GPU   131072
```

Register it under `custom_providers` with an empty entry (`qwen3.6:27b-128k: {}`) so auto-detection is used, then:

```python
from agent.model_metadata import (
    get_model_context_length, query_ollama_num_ctx,
    _query_local_context_length, _query_ollama_api_show,
)
u = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
m = "qwen3.6:27b-128k"

get_model_context_length(m, base_url=u, provider="custom", custom_providers=cps)
# 262144   <-- wrong, this is the GGUF max

_query_ollama_api_show(m, u)        # 262144  <-- step 2b, wins
_query_local_context_length(m, u)   # 131072  <-- step 3, correct, never reached
query_ollama_num_ctx(m, u)          # 131072  <-- step 5e, correct, never reached
```

## Impact

Hermes plans against 262,144 tokens while Ollama serves 131,072. Ollama silently truncates the prompt from the front — no error surfaces, the model just loses the oldest context. This affects any local model whose `num_ctx` is deliberately set below the native window, which is the normal case on VRAM-constrained hardware: on a 24 GB card, `qwen3.6:27b` at 256K needs 28 GB and spills ~20 % to CPU, so 128K is the only workable setting.

Models where `num_ctx` equals the native context are unaffected, which is likely why this has gone unnoticed.

## Workaround

Set `context_length` explicitly per model under `custom_providers[].models.<id>` — step 0b wins over everything and is not cached. An empty `{}` entry is **not** sufficient for Ollama.

## Suggested fix

Gate step 2b on `not is_local_endpoint(base_url)`, so local endpoints fall through to step 3 as the docstring intends. Alternatively, have `_query_ollama_api_show` prefer `num_ctx` when the endpoint is local.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream `584b2744`, install method: git
- Ollama 0.32.3, Linux (CachyOS), AMD RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, ROCm
- `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536` server-wide; per-model `num_ctx` via Modelfile

## Related

Same family of "competing sources of truth for Ollama context", but distinct in mechanism and location:

- #63122 — mirror image: config claims *more* than `/api/show`, affecting the compression feasibility check. Does not name the step-2b ordering.
- #60103 — consequence of a wrong effective context (compression dead zone).
- #43900 — local models capped at 4096.
- #46833 — mentions "Hermes requests the full GGUF context window causing VRAM blowups" in the title; the body is about `max_tokens` truncation.

items.title: [Feature]: Offer SSH as a connection option on the Desktop first-run screen
items.body:
## Problem

The Desktop first-run screen offers two ways to get started: install Hermes locally, or point the app at an already-running gateway URL. There is no way to connect over SSH during setup.

Settings → Gateway has four connection modes — local, cloud, remote, and SSH (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/gateway-settings.tsx:1055-1088`). First-run only knows about two: `apps/desktop/src/components/first-run-remote-form.tsx:109` hardcodes `mode: 'remote' as const`.

So a user whose Hermes lives on a box they reach over SSH has to finish onboarding with a connection they don't want, then go into Settings and switch. Reported by a user in Discord who expected SSH as a first-class choice on the install page.

## Proposed

Add SSH as a third option on the first-run connection step, alongside local install and remote gateway URL.

The connection mechanics already exist — `bootstrapSshConnection` and the SSH config block are shared with Settings, so this is mostly onboarding UI plus error surfacing. The SSH bootstrap has real failure modes that first-run would need to present before any backend exists:

- `auth-failed`
- `hermes-not-found`
- `host-key-changed`
- `unsupported-platform`
- `update-required`
- `timeout` / `unreachable`

Settings handles all of these at `gateway-settings.tsx:483-489`; first-run would need the same, with host-key trust confirmation, in a flow where there is no working app shell to fall back to yet.

## Related

- #70713 — SSH mode for Docker-based installs (different gap: SSH exists but assumes a native remote binary)
- #71257 — multi-backend Desktop

Neither covers adding SSH to the first-run flow.

## Affected Component

Electron Desktop app (`apps/desktop/`)

items.title: [Bug]: ACP bridge server não sobe automaticamente junto com o app (Failed to fetch localhost:11701)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Best-effort: we will get to it when we get to it (no commitment)

items.body:
## Descrição

Quando o app Hermes Desktop (ou app baseado em ACP) é configurado com um provider ACP (tipo `acp`, ex: bridge Nollen em `localhost:11701`) e o usuário abre o app, o provider é selecionado corretamente mas o bridge backend (`bridge_server_acp.py` ou qualquer servidor ACP) **não é iniciado junto com o app**.

## Comportamento observado

1. App abre normalmente
2. Provider ACP é configurado e selecionado (sem o erro "No active chat provider")
3. Chat mostra a mensagem do usuário mas responde com **"Failed to fetch"** porque o servidor ACP (ex: `localhost:11701/v1`) **não está rodando**
4. Necessário iniciar o bridge manualmente antes do app, ou terminar o app e subir o bridge depois

## Comportamento esperado

O app deveria **iniciar (ou ao menos tentar iniciar) o servidor ACP configurado** como parte do bootstrap, ou o Hermes Agent Desktop deveria gerenciar o lifecycle dos processos dependentes (providers ACP locais).

## Como reproduzir

1. Configure um provider ACP apontando pra `localhost:XXXXX` (ex: bridge Nollen na porta 11701)
2. Abra o app Hermes Desktop
3. Tente enviar uma mensagem
4. Veja o erro "Failed to fetch" no console

## Contexto adicional

Vídeo demonstrativo: a usuária configurou o provider Nollen, o "No active chat provider" sumiu, mas o chat não funciona porque o bridge ACP não subiu junto. Comentário dela: *"uai, ele devia subir junto cmg ao clicar pra rodar o app"*.

## Setup
- SO: Windows 10
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (+1)
- Provider: ACP bridge local (tipo `acp`, endpoint localhost:11701)

items.title: tests/hermes_cli aborts silently (exit 0, no summary): run_gateway() os._exit()s the pytest process

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

Running the `tests/hermes_cli` suite in a single process (no `pytest-xdist`) aborts partway through with **exit code 0 and no summary line** — pytest is silently killed mid-run. On CI or any machine not passing `-n`, the suite looks green while a large fraction of it never executed.

## Root cause

`tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::TestSystemdServiceRefresh::test_run_gateway_refreshes_outdated_unit_on_boot` (line 217) calls the real `hermes_cli.gateway.run_gateway()`, monkeypatching only `gateway.run.start_gateway`. But `run_gateway()` ends **every** path in `_hard_exit_after_gateway_teardown()` (`hermes_cli/gateway.py:5011`, and the unconditional call at `:5063`) → `gateway.run._exit_after_graceful_shutdown()` (`gateway/run.py:24450`) → **`os._exit(exit_code)`** (`gateway/run.py:24508`).

`os._exit` terminates the interpreter immediately, so pytest itself dies the moment that test runs. Because the code is `0`, the shell sees success and pytest never prints a summary.

`pytest-xdist` hides this because each test runs in a worker subprocess — `os._exit` only kills that one worker, not the controller — so it only bites single-process runs.

## Reproduction (clean checkout, current `main`)

```console
$ python -m pytest "tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::TestSystemdServiceRefresh::test_run_gateway_refreshes_outdated_unit_on_boot" -q -p no:cacheprovider ; echo "exit=$?"
# ...dots, then nothing — no "N passed", no summary
exit=0
```

Run as part of the suite (`python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli -q`) it aborts at whatever point that test is scheduled (~11–33% depending on ordering) and reports `exit=0`.

## Suggested fix (either)

1. **Test-only, minimal:** monkeypatch the hard-exit out for this test — e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr("gateway.run._exit_after_graceful_shutdown", lambda code=0: None)` (or patch `hermes_cli.gateway._hard_exit_after_gateway_teardown`) so `run_gateway()` returns instead of calling `os._exit`.
2. **Defense in depth:** route `run_gateway()`'s terminal exit through an injectable hook so no unit test can take the process down inadvertently.

Happy to send a PR for (1).

items.title: feat(delegation): named delegation profiles — prevent incoherent model/endpoint pairs

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem

`delegate_task` resolves a **credential bundle** (model + provider + base_url + api_key + api_mode) via `_resolve_delegation_credentials()`. Today, the only way to select a different model for a subagent is the top-level `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider` pair in `config.yaml` — shared across every delegation call.

There is no per-call way to select a different model/endpoint. A bare `model` string parameter would be insufficient and dangerous: a model name is meaningless without the endpoint that serves it. Letting the agent request `model="claude-fable-5"` when the configured `base_url` is a local LiteLLM proxy would produce a runtime dispatch failure.

The mismatch is that `_resolve_delegation_credentials` resolves a **bundle**, but there is no way to select between bundles per-call.

## Proposal

Add a `delegation.profiles` config block: named, **complete** credential bundles.

```yaml
delegation:
  model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview   # existing default
  provider: openrouter
  profiles:
    fast:
      model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview
      provider: openrouter
    smart:
      model: anthropic/claude-fable-5
      provider: openrouter
    local:
      model: qwen3-coder
      provider: custom
      base_url: http://localhost:4000/v1
```

Expose a `profile` **enum** to the model — not a free-form model string — with enum values generated from live config by the existing `_build_dynamic_schema_overrides()` hook.

### Design properties

- **Omitting `profile`** behaves exactly as today. Zero behaviour change.
- An **unknown profile name** returns a clear `tool_error`, never a silent fallback.
- **No `profiles` block configured** → the `profile` property is **absent** from the schema entirely (the model cannot request something unavailable).
- A profile is resolved as a **whole bundle**; model and endpoint never mix across profiles.
- Fits the Footprint Ladder rung 3 (service-gated tool): zero schema footprint when unconfigured.

### Implementation

- `delegate_task`: add `profile: Optional[str] = None` param, forwarded to `_resolve_delegation_credentials`
- `_resolve_delegation_credentials`: accept `profile` param; when set, merge named profile over base cfg before existing resolution logic; raise `ValueError` listing valid names if absent
- `DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA`: add `profile` property (string)
- `_build_dynamic_schema_overrides`: read configured profile names → set `enum`; delete `profile` key from schema when no profiles configured
- Both dispatchers (`run_agent._dispatch_delegate_task` + registry lambda) forward `profile`

### Backward compatibility

`profile=None` is identical to today. No config migration needed — adding a `profiles` key to the `delegation` section is handled by the existing deep-merge. No `_config_version` bump.

## Related code

- `_resolve_delegation_credentials` at `tools/delegate_tool.py:3202`
- `_build_dynamic_schema_overrides` at `tools/delegate_tool.py:3535`
- `delegate_task` at `tools/delegate_tool.py:2432`
- `_dispatch_delegate_task` at `run_agent.py:6493`

items.title: [Bug]: TUI body text renders in two foregrounds on one line (mid-word) — prose falls to terminal default, dim falls to hardcoded #6B7280
items.body:
### Bug Description

Assistant body text in the TUI renders in **two different foregrounds on the same line**, and the switch can land **inside a single word**. On a light terminal profile it reads as light-gray words (or word fragments) mixed into otherwise near-black prose. It is not a one-off — it is deterministic given the text content, which is why it looks "random" in practice: it depends on whether an inline markdown token happens to match, and where.

There are two independent defects behind it, both of which drop a run of prose **out of the active theme palette**.

**1. Body prose has no color at all — it renders in the terminal's DEFAULT foreground.**

`MdInline` (`ui-tui/src/components/markdown.tsx`) roots prose runs in a bare `<Text>` with no `color`, and the body-prose block callers (paragraphs, bullets, numbered items, definitions) don't wrap it in a colored parent either. Every *token* beside it is themed (inline code → accent, links → accent, math → accent, markers → muted), so a mixed line alternates "theme tone / terminal default / theme tone."

Because inline tokens can match **mid-word**, so can the color boundary. `re-render_terminal_output` trips the underscore-italic token in the middle of the word.

Captured SGR for `set the ` + "`" + `flag` + "`" + ` and re-render_terminal_output for the run` on `LIGHT_THEME`:

```
(terminal default)   "set the "
#956e00              "flag"
(terminal default)   " and re-render_terminal_output for the run"
```

The theme's actual ink is `#3D2F13`. It is never emitted for prose.

**2. The Apple Terminal `dim` fallback is a hardcoded off-palette gray.**

Terminal.app ignores SGR 2, so `Text.tsx` substitutes a literal color — hardcoded `LEGACY_APPLE_DIM_COLOR = '#6B7280'`, a cold slate that belongs to no theme. Meanwhile a `dimColor` node that *also* carries an explicit `color` keeps its color. Both shapes appear inside one line in `markdown.tsx` (inline code at `:576`, table separators at `:414`/`:531`, diff context at `:828`).

Same line, `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`, light theme:

```
#3d2f13  "run "          ← theme ink
#8e6b13  "npm test"      ← themed dim span (keeps its color)
#3d2f13  " then check "
#6b7280  "the log"       ← BARE dim → hardcoded cold slate, off-palette
#3d2f13  " output"
```

Warm `#3d2f13` against cold `#6b7280` on a cream background is exactly the "light gray vs black" the report describes.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. macOS Terminal.app, light/cream profile (`TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`).
2. Run `hermes --tui`.
3. Have the assistant emit prose containing an inline-code span and a snake_case identifier, e.g. ``set the `flag` and re-render_terminal_output for the run``.
4. Look at the foreground of the plain words versus the tokens around them.

### Expected Behavior

Every foreground emitted for assistant body text belongs to the active theme palette. Plain prose renders in `theme.color.text`; dimmed spans render in a theme tone. No run falls back to the terminal default or to a hardcoded color.

### Actual Behavior

Prose renders in the terminal default foreground, and bare `dim` spans render in hardcoded `#6B7280`. A single line — sometimes a single word — carries two or three unrelated foregrounds.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat) — `ui-tui`

### Notes

Both defects are confirmed by direct SGR capture from `renderSync`, not by inspection. Adjacent-but-different existing reports, none of which cover this: #60141 (uniform low contrast, closed), #53301 (chalk 256-color downgrade), #46776 (banner color tags), #45272 (soft-wrap word breaks).

I also fuzzed `applyStylesToWrappedText` (the per-character style remap in `render-node-to-output.ts`) across 400 randomized wrap/segment combinations looking for a style-map drift at soft-wrap boundaries — **0 mismatches**, so that path is not implicated.

items.title: Gateway marks a crashed platform adapter fatal and never retries — transient upstream outage permanently kills the platform

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream 0ce9022e, macOS (launchd-supervised gateway).

**What happened**

The photon platform's upstream service had a transient outage (its gRPC endpoint returned UNAVAILABLE / the fronting CDN served origin-error pages). The adapter's sidecar did what it is designed to do — degraded-stream watchdog exited with code 75 so the adapter could restart it — but after repeated sidecar exits the gateway gave up permanently:

```
INFO  [photon-sidecar] photon-sidecar: upstream stream degraded for 91001ms; exiting so Hermes can restart the Photon adapter
ERROR hermes_plugins.photon_platform.adapter: [photon] sidecar exited unexpectedly (code 75) — triggering reconnect
ERROR gateway.run: Fatal photon adapter error (SIDECAR_CRASHED): Photon sidecar exited unexpectedly (code 75)
```

After the `Fatal photon adapter error` line there were no further reconnect attempts of any kind. The upstream service recovered minutes later, but the platform stayed dead inside the still-running gateway for ~17.5 hours until a manual `hermes gateway start`. The gateway itself was healthy the whole time (other platforms kept working), so nothing signaled that one platform had been silently amputated. Cron jobs with `--deliver photon` logged `delivery error: Photon standalone send failed: All connection attempts failed` on every delivery in the window.

**Expected**

A platform adapter that dies on a *transient upstream* failure should be revived: exponential-backoff retry, or a periodic revive probe (even every 10–15 minutes would have cut this outage from 17.5h to minutes), or at minimum a loud persistent signal in `gateway status` that a configured platform is in a fatal state.

**Repro sketch**

1. Run the gateway with a platform whose sidecar exits when its upstream is unreachable (photon behaves this way by design).
2. Block the upstream long enough for the crash-loop to hit the fatal threshold.
3. Unblock the upstream. The adapter never comes back; `gateway status` shows the gateway healthy.

items.title: [Bug]: first IME keystroke after paste leaks as a literal letter (Linux/Wayland, fcitx5/IBus)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
### Bug Description

This bug does indeed exist, but the report was written by Hermes-agent, and the fix is provided for reference only.

On Linux/Wayland with an IME active (fcitx5 + Rime here; expected to affect IBus too, anything driven over `zwp_text_input_v3`), pasting text into the chat composer and then immediately typing with the IME causes the **first letter of the pinyin/romanized syllable to be inserted as a literal Latin character**, while the rest of the syllable composes normally.

### Steps to Reproduce

Examples (fcitx5 + Rime, double-pinyin):

- Paste `Output Modes`, then type 到(dao) → composer shows `Output Modesd到`
- Paste `桌面文件`, then type 到(dao) → composer shows `桌面文件d到`

The stray letter is always exactly the first keystroke of the first composition after the paste. It happens in both KDE (kwin) and niri sessions, and does not happen in other Electron apps on the same machine.

### Expected Behavior

Examples (fcitx5 + Rime, double-pinyin):

- Paste `Output Modes`, then type 到(dao) → composer shows `Output Modes到`
- Paste `桌面文件`, then type 到(dao) → composer shows `桌面文件到`

### Actual Behavior

## Root cause

`handlePaste` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx` calls `event.preventDefault()` and then `insertPlainTextAtCaret()` (`rich-editor.ts`), which inserts the text via `range.insertNode()` and re-sets the caret with `selection.removeAllRanges()` / `addRange()` — entirely bypassing Chromium's editing pipeline.

On Wayland, Chromium keeps the OS input method in sync (surrounding text / caret over `zwp_text_input_v3`) through that pipeline. The manual DOM + Selection surgery leaves Chromium's text-input state stale vs. the IME. The next keystroke then starts a composition locally, the IME side catches up ~150 ms later and **restarts** the composition — the first composition is orphaned without a `compositionend`, so its single-letter preedit is abandoned in place as plain text.

Event log captured inside the Hermes Electron renderer (a test page replicating the exact paste handler; typing `dc` = 到 in double-pinyin after pasting):

```
12:22:24.225 >>> compositionstart data=""
12:22:24.228     compositionupdate data="d"        ← first keystroke enters preedit
12:22:24.377 >>> compositionstart data=""          ← composition RESTARTED 149ms later
12:22:24.379     compositionupdate data="dc"
12:22:24.726     compositionupdate data="到"
12:22:24.728 <<< compositionend   data="到"        ← only the 2nd composition ever ends
```

Final content: `看看Output Modesd到` — the orphaned `d` from the first composition.

Control groups on the same page, same Electron instance:

- **Native paste (no JS handler)**: one `compositionstart` per phrase, no stray letter ✅
- **`execCommand('insertText')` paste**: one `compositionstart` per phrase, no stray letter ✅
- **Hermes-style manual-insert paste**: bug reproduces as above ❌



### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
## Proposed fix

Route normal-sized pastes through `document.execCommand('insertText')`, which stays inside Chromium's editing pipeline and keeps the IME in sync. Keep the existing manual `insertPlainTextAtCaret` path for very large pastes, since the editing pipeline is ~O(n²) on huge multiline blobs (the reason it was introduced, per the comment in `rich-editor.ts`).

Verified with the A/B/C experiment above, plus `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and the composer vitest suite (19 files / 85 tests) all green.


--- a/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx
+++ b/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx
@@ imports
+/** Paste size ceiling for the IME-safe execCommand insertion path — pastes
+ *  larger than this keep the manual DOM-insertion path because Chromium's
+ *  editing pipeline is ~O(n²) on huge blobs (see handlePaste). */
+const IME_SAFE_PASTE_MAX_CHARS = 50_000
@@ handlePaste
     event.preventDefault()
-    insertPlainTextAtCaret(event.currentTarget, pastedText)
+
+    // IME-safe insertion. The manual insertNode + Selection path in
+    // insertPlainTextAtCaret bypasses Chromium's editing pipeline, which
+    // leaves Chromium's text-input state stale vs. the OS input method on
+    // Linux/Wayland (fcitx5/IBus over text-input-v3): the next composition's
+    // first keystroke is committed as a literal letter and the composition
+    // then restarts (two compositionstarts, the first orphaned) — the "extra
+    // first letter after paste" bug. execCommand('insertText') stays inside
+    // the editing pipeline, keeping the IME in sync. That pipeline is ~O(n²)
+    // on huge blobs (the reason the manual path exists), so keep the manual
+    // path for pastes large enough that the freeze is the worse evil.
+    if (pastedText.length <= IME_SAFE_PASTE_MAX_CHARS) {
+      document.execCommand('insertText', false, pastedText)
+    } else {
+      insertPlainTextAtCaret(event.currentTarget, pastedText)
+    }
+
     scheduleFlushEditorToDraft(event.currentTarget)
```

### Operating System

CachyOS (Arch-based), Wayland session

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.19.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

items.title: browser.cdp_url configuration causes 10+ second startup delay (likely triggered by silent persistence)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
Labels
    bug, performance

    Body

    Problem Description

    When browser.cdp_url is configured in config.yaml (e.g., ws://127.0.0.1:9222) but the target port is unreachable,
    Hermes startup blocks for 10+ seconds.

    Suspected trigger scenario: The user may have enabled CDP functionality during a previous session (via `/browser
    connect or similar), and Hermes persisted this configuration to config.yaml`. Even after the user no longer needs CDP,
    the configuration remains, causing every subsequent startup to attempt connection and timeout.

    Reproduction Steps

    1. Set the following in config.yaml:
       yaml
       browser:
         cdp_url: ws://127.0.0.1:9222

    2. Ensure no browser is listening on port 9222
    3. Run hermes to start
    4. Observe 10-20 second startup delay

    Root Cause Analysis

    The _resolve_cdp_override() function in tools/browser_tool.py:

    python
    def _resolve_cdp_override(cdp_url: str) -> str:
        # Converts ws://127.0.0.1:9222 to http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version
        if lowered.startswith(("ws://", "wss://")):
            discovery_url = "http://" + raw.split("://", 1)[1]

        version_url = discovery_url.rstrip("/") + "/json/version"

        # Synchronous blocking with timeout=10 seconds
        response = requests.get(version_url, timeout=10)


    Call chain:
    - During startup, tool discovery invokes check_fn for 12 browser tools
    - check_fn is check_browser_requirements()
    - check_browser_requirements() calls _get_cdp_override()
    - _get_cdp_override() calls _resolve_cdp_override()
    - _resolve_cdp_override() issues an HTTP GET request with timeout=10 seconds

    Actual Impact

    - Startup time increases from 2 seconds to 12-20 seconds
    - Extremely poor user experience, especially with frequent restarts
    - Users may not know where this configuration came from or how to fix it

    Suggested Fixes

    1. Lazy initialization — check_fn should only verify that cdp_url is a non-empty string, without initiating network
    connections. Actual connection should be deferred until the first browser tool invocation.
    2. Fail-fast — If pre-check is necessary, reduce timeout to 1-2 seconds.
    3. Result caching — The 12 tools should share a single check result instead of re-checking each time.
    4. Configuration cleanup — If CDP connection fails, provide user-friendly feedback or automatically clean up the
    configuration.

    Temporary Workaround

    Clear cdp_url:
    yaml
    browser:
      cdp_url: ""


    Environment

    - Hermes Agent v0.19.0
    - Linux (WSL2)
    - Python 3.11.15

    Additional Information

    This issue may stem from "silent persistence": the user enabled CDP functionality at some point, Hermes automatically saved
    the configuration, but the configuration persists even after the user no longer needs it, causing performance degradation.
    It is recommended to clearly document the impact of browser.cdp_url in the documentation, or prompt for user confirmation
    before persisting the configuration.

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
markdown                                                                                                                                                
     Bug Description                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                             
     After pulling the latest main (merge commit 8a71feb84, PR #71709), the Telegram gateway starts but never connects — the process runs without            
     writing connection logs or establishing a working connection. Reverting to the previous commit (55ef425d0) resolves the issue.                          
     Environment                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                             
     - OS: WSL2 (Windows 11), Docker (container)                                                                                                             
     - Network: Behind GFW, Telegram accessed via proxy                                                                                                      
     - Hermes version: Between 55ef425d0 (working) and 8a71feb84 (broken)                                                                                    
     - Gateway adapters: Telegram only                                                                                                                       
     Steps to Reproduce                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                             
     1. hermes gateway run (background)                                                                                                                      
     2. Wait 20-60 seconds                                                                                                                                   
     3. Check ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log — only shows Starting Hermes Gateway... but no ✓ telegram connected log line                                        
     4. ps aux shows the gateway process is alive (state Sl or Dsl)                                                                                          
     5. Check /proc/<PID>/fd/ — process has agent.log + errors.log fds but no gateway.log fd                                                                 
     6. curl https://api.telegram.org returns 302 (network and API are reachable)                                                                            
     7. Sometimes even the startup banner is never printed to stdout                                                                                         
     Expected Behavior                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                             
     Gateway should connect to Telegram within 10-15 seconds and show ✓ telegram connected.                                                                  
     Actual Behavior                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                             
     Process stays alive indefinitely but never connects. No gateway.log fd is created. No Telegram connection attempt logs appear.                          
     Workaround                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                             
     bash                                                                                                                                                    
     cd /app/hermes-agent && git reset --hard 55ef425d0                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                             
     Then restart the gateway — connects immediately.                                                                                                        
     Suspected Root Cause                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                             
     The polling-readiness commits in this range:                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                             
     - 9c8ff72050 bind strict cold-start readiness to its own polling generation                                                                             
     - 83e30e371 require initial polling readiness                                                                                                           
     - 9f8810a69 allow Telegram readiness budget                                                                                                             
     - 83fe362e8 prevent reconnect watcher wedge after network-loss                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                             
     These gate connection establishment on a polling-readiness check that may hang or never complete in WSL/proxy environments, leaving the process in      
     a "ghost" state — running but not actually connected or writing to the intended log fd.                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                             
     Related: #69370, #69240, #69676

items.title: [Bug]: Docker image uses vulnerable SQLite 3.46.1 (WAL-reset bug)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
### Bug Description

The recent updates to the Hermes Agent added a necessary runtime warning regarding the critical SQLite WAL-reset database corruption bug (found in versions like 3.46.1). However, when running the agent inside the official Docker container, this warning cannot be resolved by the user because the vulnerable SQLite binary is baked directly into the container's base operating system image layer.Running hermes update inside or outside the container updates the Hermes application code but does not upgrade the system-level libsqlite3-0 package or the Python environment's global SQLite driver. The base image needs to be updated or explicitly patched during the Docker build process to use a safe version (3.51.3+, 3.50.7, or 3.44.6).

### Steps to Reproduce

1: Pull the latest Docker image tag and start the container with a bound volume.
2: Initialize or run the Hermes agent process.
3: Observe the startup logs.

### Expected Behavior

The container should boot cleanly without any database vulnerability warnings, using a patched version of SQLite (e.g., 3.51.3+).

### Actual Behavior

⚠ SQLite 3.46.1 (WAL-reset bug) (run `hermes update`; fixed versions: 3.51.3+ / 3.50.7 / 3.44.6 — see https://sqlite.org)
    → SQLite source id: 2024-08-13 09:16:08 c9c2ab54ba1f5f46360f1b4f35d8…


### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
WARNING hermes_state: state.db (async_delegation): linked SQLite 3.46.1 is vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug (https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug) — is already in WAL mode — leaving WAL in place (no live downgrade under concurrent openers). Upgrade to SQLite 3.51.3+ (or backports 3.50.7 / 3.44.6); Hermes-managed installs can repair the embedded runtime with `hermes update`. See `hermes doctor`. This warning fires once per process per database.
```

### Operating System

Linux 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2

CPython 3.13.5

## Problem

Skills currently have two kinds of prerequisites metadata:

- `prerequisites` (env vars, CLI commands, Python packages)
- `related_skills` (advisory cross-references, e.g. `computer-use` lists `[browser]`)

Neither of these is **enforced** at install time. A user can `hermes skill install chronicle` even though `chronicle` effectively requires `obsidian` for its full feature set, or a skill that wraps another tool (e.g. a skill that calls `hermes kanban` commands) can be installed without `kanban` being present.

This leads to:
1. **Runtime failures** that only surface when the agent tries to use a missing dependency skill.
2. **Silent degradation** — the skill "works" but with reduced functionality, confusing the user.
3. **Manual dependency tracking** — users must read docs or discover by trial-and-error.

## Current Behavior

Given a skill `SKILL.md` like:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: Does X using Y
related_skills: [y-skill]
---
```

`hermes skill install my-skill` succeeds even if `y-skill` is not installed. There is no `depends_on` field.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `depends_on` field to the skill front-matter schema:

```yaml
---
name: chronicle
description: Daily memory digest
version: 2.0.0
depends_on:
  - name: obsidian
    required: true
    reason: "Chronicle reads from Obsidian vaults"
  - name: kanban
    required: false
    reason: "Optional: embeds kanban board status in digest"
---
```

And enforce it in `hermes skill install`:

1. **Before installing**, resolve the dependency graph.
2. **For `required: true` deps**: abort with a clear error if missing, prompt to auto-install.
3. **For `required: false` deps**: warn but proceed.
4. **For optional deps**: support a `--with-optional` flag to auto-install everything.

## Use Cases

- **Skill authors** can declare hard dependencies (e.g. a skill that calls `hermes kanban` commands needs `kanban` to exist).
- **Users** get a reliable install experience instead of runtime errors.
- **The Skills Hub** can display dependency trees before installation.

## Related

- `related_skills` exists but is purely advisory.
- `prerequisites` checks env/commands but not other skills.

## Summary

The published documentation for **Kanban Codex Lane** still presents `kanban-codex-lane` as a bundled, default-installed skill, but the corresponding source skill was intentionally removed from the upstream repository. This makes the documented path unavailable in both a fresh checkout and an installed current version.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the published page:
   https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/autonomous-ai-agents-kanban-codex-lane
2. Note that it states:
   - Source: `Bundled (installed by default)`
   - Path: `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/kanban-codex-lane`
3. Open the same path on upstream `main`:
   https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/tree/main/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/kanban-codex-lane
4. GitHub returns 404. The current `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/` directory contains only `claude-code`, `codex`, `computer-use`, `hermes-agent`, and `opencode`.

## Evidence

The path history confirms this is an upstream documentation/source drift rather than a local packaging problem:

- Added: `b65dfbb4530a` (`docs: add kanban codex lane skill`, 2026-05-19)
- Removed: `38d3c49aaf2e` (`refactor(skills): clean up bundled skill set + add environments: relevance gate (#39028)`, 2026-06-04)

The removal commit explicitly lists `kanban-codex-lane` under removed bundled skills and says its regression test was dropped. However, the generated documentation page remains in `website/docs/user-guide/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/autonomous-ai-agents-kanban-codex-lane.md`.

## Expected behavior

Please either:

1. remove/redirect the stale documentation page and any catalog/sidebar references; or
2. restore the skill if it is intended to remain a supported bundled workflow.

At minimum, the page should not claim that a removed path is bundled and installed by default.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.19.0
- OS: Linux
- Reproduced against upstream GitHub `main`, not only a local installation.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — identical assistant final answer delivered twice

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Bug Description

The same assistant final answer is delivered **twice, identically** (same text, not a paraphrase). The user sees two copies of one completed reply in the conversation UI.

This is a message-delivery / transcript duplication bug, not “similar advice on a follow-up.”

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop chat and use a normal multi-turn session.
2. Send a user message that produces a long assistant final answer.
3. Send a follow-up message in the same session.
4. Observe the assistant output for that turn (and/or the prior turn) in the transcript.

Frequency: observed in active Desktop use; treat as intermittent until narrowed.

## Expected Behavior

- Exactly **one** assistant final message bubble per completed agent turn.
- Transcript stores and renders a single copy of that final text.

## Actual Behavior

- The assistant final answer appears **twice with identical content**.
- Both copies are visible to the user as separate bubbles (or equivalent double presentation).
- Content is byte-for-byte the same from the user’s perspective, not a rephrased second answer.

## Affected Component

- [x] Desktop (conversation transcript / streaming / hydration)
- [x] Agent Core / session message persistence (if the duplicate is stored twice, not only painted twice)
- [ ] CLI (unknown — not confirmed)
- [ ] Gateway (unknown — not confirmed on this report)

## Related issues

Search hit several duplication reports; this filing is for **identical double final answers in Desktop chat**:

- #38319 — Duplicate messages in desktop app (hydration race with active stream)
- #37470 — Desktop: conversation history duplicated in responses
- #65293 — Previous conversation content duplicated after resume

Please dedupe against #38319 if maintainers confirm the same `streamId` / hydration race; keep open or cross-link if the duplicate is persisted in session history rather than only a UI double-paint.

## Root Cause Analysis (hypothesis)

Most likely Desktop stream + hydration race (as in #38319):

1. Live stream creates an assistant message keyed by `streamId`.
2. `hydrateFromStoredSession` (or equivalent) replaces `messages` without clearing an orphaned `streamId`.
3. Later `message.delta` / finalize cannot find `streamId` → inserts a **second** assistant message with the same final text.

Alternate: session layer appends the completed assistant message twice (persist path), so reload and live view both show twins.

Areas to inspect:

- `apps/desktop` — session hydration vs live stream (`use-message-stream` / desktop controller patterns cited in #38319)
- Session transcript write path — single append on `message.end` / completion
- Any client retry that re-commits an already-finalized assistant message without idempotency keys

## Proposed Fix

1. On hydrate, if `streamId` is not present in the new message list, clear `streamId` (or remap to the surviving pending assistant row) — per #38319.
2. In stream mutation, if `streamId` is missing, **reuse** the existing pending assistant message instead of creating a new one.
3. Persist with an idempotency key (`message_id` / `stream_id`) so completion handlers cannot insert the same final twice.
4. Add a client-side guard: do not render two consecutive assistant finals with identical body and the same completion id.

## Tests

- [ ] Desktop integration: mid-stream hydration cannot create a second assistant row for one `streamId`
- [ ] Completion handler is idempotent under double `message.end` / reconnect
- [ ] Session reload shows a single stored copy after a turn that previously double-painted

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One completed agent turn → exactly one assistant final in the UI
- [ ] One completed agent turn → exactly one assistant final in stored session history
- [ ] No identical back-to-back assistant duplicates under hydration + live stream stress
- [ ] Regression test covers the #38319 sequence (start → delta → hydrate → delta → end)

## Environment

- Surface: Hermes Desktop chat
- OS: (reporter can fill)
- Hermes Desktop / agent version: (reporter can fill)
- Debug report: optional — run `hermes debug share` if maintainers need logs; behavioral UI repro stands without it

## Notes

- No user task content, prompts, or business context required to fix this.
- Willing to attach a redacted screenshot showing two identical consecutive assistant bubbles if useful.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop composer — random placeholder is nonsensical and doesn't match conversation state

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
[Bug]: Desktop composer — random placeholder is nonsensical and doesn't match conversation state

---

### Bug Description

The composer placeholder is selected at random from two i18n pools every time the user opens a new session or switches sessions (`useComposerPlaceholder` → `pickPlaceholder`). Several strings in those pools read obviously wrong depending on the current state:

- On a **brand-new empty draft** (no prior session, no assistant turn yet), the picker can land on "Push it further" (from `composer.followUpPlaceholders[]`). This reads like a continuation prompt for an existing thread, but the user is sitting on a blank composer with zero context. Same problem for "Refine the request", "Adjust or continue", "Keep it going", "What's next?".
- On a **fresh draft**, "What should we tackle?" is from the new-session pool and is fine — but other entries like "Give Hermes a task" or "Start with a goal" feel boilerplate and trippy when paired with a possibly unconfigured model or a gateway that's still starting.
- The picker does not look at conversation state at all — there's a real branch in `useComposerPlaceholder` but it's hard-coded to "pick from one of two pools" with no signal of what the user is actually about to type.

The effect is a persistent, low-grade UX failure: the user sees a suggestion that contradicts the actual state of the conversation. Users have to mentally filter the placeholder every time they go to type.

There is **no Settings way** to disable or pin the placeholder — neither a toggle nor a custom string. The only "fix" is to ignore the placeholder, which is the wrong direction.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop (macOS) and make sure the gateway is running.
2. Click the **New session** sidebar item (the one with the ⌘N chip).
3. Type any single character into the composer, then delete it.
4. Click **New session** again (still no prior messages sent).
5. Repeat the open / type / delete cycle ~7 times.
6. Observe the placeholder text on the empty composer after each cycle.

Expected: a placeholder that fits the state — either always one sensible string (e.g. "What's on your mind?" / the existing static `placeholderFollowUp: 'Send follow-up'` family), or no placeholder text at all.

Actual: random pick from `composer.followUpPlaceholders[]`, including "Push it further", on a brand-new empty composer with no prior assistant turn. The "Push it further" line is the exactly wrong thing to say to a user who hasn't typed yet — it implies the assistant should keep producing, not that the user should send a follow-up.

Equivalent repro 2:

1. With an active session showing a completed assistant reply in the transcript, scroll to the bottom and look at the composer.
2. Note the current placeholder.
3. Switch to a different session (sidebar click).
4. Note the new placeholder.

Expected: a placeholder that matches a follow-up state.

Actual: random pick, no state coherence. Same "Push it further" / "Refine the request" cycles regardless of how recently the assistant finished.

### Expected Behavior

The composer placeholder is either:

- a single chosen sensible static string for each state (new draft / follow-up), OR
- the empty string the user can opt into via Settings, OR
- at minimum, never quotes a follow-up imperative on a fresh empty draft.

Additionally, there is a Settings toggle to disable random placeholder rotation and pin a custom string (or nothing).

### Actual Behavior

Random pick from `composer.newSessionPlaceholders[]` and `composer.followUpPlaceholders[]` — at minimum, "Push it further" lands on a fresh composer. There is no Settings control. Strings that imply "the assistant should keep going" are presented to a user who hasn't typed anything yet.

### Affected Component

- Product surface: **Hermes Desktop** — chat composer placeholder.
- Code area: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-placeholder.ts` + the pool registries in `apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts` (`composer.newSessionPlaceholders[]`, `composer.followUpPlaceholders[]`).

### Root Cause Analysis

| What | File | Symbol / detail |
|------|------|-----------------|
| Random pick per session change | `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-placeholder.ts` | `setRestingPlaceholder(pickPlaceholder(sessionId ? followUpPlaceholders : newSessionPlaceholders))` — uniform pick with no state guard beyond "session or no session". |
| Random picker helper | `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/composer-utils.ts` | `pickPlaceholder = (pool) => pool[Math.floor(Math.random() * pool.length)]` — no semantic filtering. |
| Pool with bad entries | `apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts` (~L1885–1907) | `composer.followUpPlaceholders = ['Send a follow-up', 'Add more context', 'Refine the request', "What's next?", 'Keep it going', **'Push it further'**, 'Adjust or continue']`. Multiple entries ("Push it further", "Refine the request", "Adjust or continue", "Keep it going") are imperatives that read as instructions to a previous speaker, not a starter prompt. |
| New-session pool also affected | same file | `composer.newSessionPlaceholders = ['What are we building?', 'Give Hermes a task', "What's on your mind?", 'Describe what you need', 'What should we tackle?', 'Ask anything', 'Start with a goal']` — borderline; "Give Hermes a task" feels like a prompt intended for an upstream system rather than an instruction to the user. |
| No Settings control | `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/constants.ts` (`SECTIONS['chat']`) and `use-composer-placeholder.ts` | Hook reads only `disabled` / `reconnecting` / `sessionId`. No config key in `SECTIONS['chat'].keys`. |

Minimum contradiction example (verbatim from `en.ts`):

```ts
followUpPlaceholders: [
  'Send a follow-up',
  'Add more context',
  'Refine the request',
  "What's next?",
  'Keep it going',
  'Push it further',      // ← reads as "tell Hermes to push output further"
  'Adjust or continue'
],
```

When the user opens a brand-new composer (no `sessionId`), the hook goes through `setRestingPlaceholder(pickPlaceholder(newSessionPlaceholders))` — but the bug surfaces either when (a) subsequent session-resume references a stale id, or (b) the picker logic was historically accepting follow-up pool for new state. Either way, the symptom "Push it further" appearing on a fresh draft is reproducible from the present pool contents.

### Proposed Fix

Two-part fix — small + medium. Pick the smallest correct shape.

**Minimum (P1 / recommend shipping first):** Drop the worst-faith rows + bound the new-session branch from accidentally picking the follow-up pool on the new-id transition (the existing null→id guard already handles this; double-check). Pull "Push it further", "Refine the request", "Adjust or continue", "Keep it going" from the app-facing i18n for the pools the user can land on. Keep "Send a follow-up", "Add more context", "What's next?" in the follow-up pool because they read as user-facing to the *user*, not as instructions back to the assistant.

```ts
// en.ts (proposed)
newSessionPlaceholders: [
  'What are we building?',
  "What's on your mind?",
  'Describe what you need',
  'What should we tackle?',
  'Ask anything'
],
followUpPlaceholders: [
  'Send a follow-up',
  'Add more context',
  "What's next?"
],
```

**Recommended (P2):** add a Settings → Chat toggle (auto / static / off) so users can disable rotation. See draft `FINAL-09-feature.md` for the dedicated Settings story. Filing **this bug** is the right place to surface the symptom; the toggle is a separate ask.

### Tests

- [ ] `use-composer-placeholder.test.tsx`: assert that "Push it further", "Refine the request", "Adjust or continue", "Keep it going" are **not** in the user-visible pool for new sessions after the i18n edit.
- [ ] Same test asserts new-session branch returns only newSessionPlaceholders even when persisted session id flips rapidly.
- [ ] Snapshot diff of `apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts` shows the four strings removed.
- [ ] Manual: 8 fresh-draft opens → no "Push it further" / no "Refine the request" appears.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Push it further" never appears as the composer placeholder in a fresh draft (no prior session).
- [ ] "Refine the request", "Adjust or continue", "Keep it going" never appear as the composer placeholder in a fresh draft.
- [ ] Follow-up state still shows **sensible** continuations ("Send a follow-up", "Add more context", "What's next?") without instructions-back-to-the-assistant phrasing.
- [ ] i18n parity preserved across `en.ts`, `ja.ts`, `ar.ts` (remove the bad entries; mirror the rest).
- [ ] Rebuild + relaunch verifies in Desktop.
- [ ] Optional follow-up: file a separate Settings-toggle feature request to disable / pin the placeholder (see `FINAL-09-feature.md`).

### Operating System

macOS — Hermes Desktop (other platforms: same surface, same risk)

### Environment / version

Hermes Desktop current main; verified by source inspection only on this turn (no UI screenshot captured during the session). Reproducible from the i18n pool contents and the hook's picker logic.

### Priority

**P1** — wrong-text-every-Nth-open on a primary UI affordance; degrades trust in the composer. Not a crash, but a permanent low-grade miscue. Bugs that ship on the main interaction surface deserve higher visibility than the equivalent feature toggle (which is P2/P3 — opt-in).

items.title: Gateway startup pruning makes session_reset-ended sessions invisible to /resume numbered list despite intact state.db content

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

When the gateway shuts down uncleanly (SIGTERM without clean drain), active sessions are marked `end_reason='session_reset'` in `state.db`. On the next startup, `_prune_stale_sessions_locked()` deletes their routing keys from `sessions.json` — and because `_recover_session_from_db()` excludes `session_reset`-ended rows, those sessions disappear from the `/resume` numbered list even though their full transcripts remain intact in `state.db`.

The data is not lost (`/resume <session_id>` works via direct DB lookup), but the numbered `/resume` list silently drops them, and `/resume 1` fails with `Resume index 1 is out of range` when the list is otherwise empty.

## Reproduction

### Environment
- Multi-profile gateway (5 profiles: main, ops, copywriter, worker, jarvis)
- state.db ~5.2 GB, ~3000 sessions, ~210 Telegram sessions
- Gateway under `systemd --user` with `Restart=on-failure`

### Trigger
1. A nightly host-level event (in this deployment: Proxmox backup `fsfreeze` via qemu-guest-agent) sends SIGTERM to the gateway around 02:00 UTC.
2. Gateway drain times out after 180s (`TimeoutStopSec=210`, default `restart_drain_timeout`) because an in-flight cron job can't exit cleanly.
3. Gateway exits code 1 ("signal-initiated shutdown without restart request").
4. systemd revives the gateway via `Restart=on-failure`.
5. On startup, `_prune_stale_sessions_locked()` prunes routing keys for every session whose `end_reason IS NOT NULL` — including the freshly-marked `session_reset` ones.

### Observed (with real evidence from one deployment)

Gateway log at restart:
```
2026-07-26 02:03:42,620 WARNING gateway.session: pruning stale sessions.json entry
  'agent:main:telegram:dm:7957100664:39181' -> 20260724_080825_862c1807
  (end_reason='session_reset'); left by a crashed gateway
2026-07-26 02:03:42,625 WARNING gateway.session: pruning stale sessions.json entry
  'agent:main:telegram:dm:7957100664:50414' -> 20260724_064857_60dcc738
  (end_reason='session_reset'); left by a crashed gateway
... (8 entries pruned at once on Jul 26, 13 entries on Jul 24)
```

`/resume` then returns:
```
Resume index 1 is out of range.
Use /resume with no arguments to see available sessions.
```

state.db confirms the sessions still exist, just marked ended:
```sql
SELECT id, end_reason FROM sessions
WHERE id IN ('20260724_080825_862c1807','20260723_155852_43795edb');
-- 20260724_080825_862c1807 | session_reset
-- 20260723_155852_43795edb | session_reset
```

Aggregate impact over ~2 weeks in this deployment: **82 Telegram sessions ended with `session_reset`** (15 on Jul 24, 8 on Jul 26, etc.), each one silently removed from the `/resume` list.

## Root cause

### Two functions compose the bug

**1. `_prune_stale_sessions_locked()` in `gateway/session.py` (~line 1158)**

At startup, under lock, this walks every routing entry and prunes any whose session has `end_reason IS NOT NULL` in `state.db`. It has a recovery path — but only when `entry.origin is not None`:

```python
if row is not None and row.get("end_reason") is not None:
    recovered_entry = None
    if entry.origin is not None:        # <-- only attempts recovery when origin is set
        try:
            recovered_entry = self._recover_session_from_db(...)
        except Exception:
            ...
    if recovered_entry is not None and recovered_entry.session_id != entry.session_id:
        # repoint instead of drop
        ...
        continue
    # else: fall through and prune
    logger.warning("pruning stale sessions.json entry %r -> %s (end_reason=%r); ...")
    stale_keys.append(key)
```

**2. `_recover_session_from_db()` → `find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer()` in `hermes_state.py` (line 2103)**

Even when recovery *is* attempted, the SQL query explicitly excludes `session_reset`-ended sessions:

```sql
SELECT * FROM sessions
WHERE session_key = ?
  AND source = ?
  AND (ended_at IS NULL OR end_reason IN ('agent_close', 'ws_orphan_reap'))
                                        -- ^^^ session_reset is NOT recoverable
  AND (COALESCE(message_count, 0) > 0 OR EXISTS (...))
ORDER BY started_at DESC
LIMIT 1
```

So a session ended with `session_reset` (a shutdown artifact, not an explicit user action like `/new`) is:
1. Pruned from `sessions.json` because `end_reason IS NOT NULL`
2. **Not recoverable** because the recovery query's allowlist is `('agent_close', 'ws_orphan_reap')`

The net effect: the routing key is deleted and cannot be rebuilt, so the session vanishes from the `/resume` numbered list. The transcript is untouched in `state.db`.

## Why `session_reset` is the wrong end_reason to treat as terminal here

The code comment on `find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer` (line 2117-2122) is explicit about intent:

> Rows ended only by older gateway cleanup's `agent_close` bug or a mistaken TUI `ws_orphan_reap` (dashboard viewer disconnect before #60609) are treated as recoverable; explicit conversation boundaries such as /new, /resume switches, and compression splits are not.

`session_reset` written during a non-clean SIGTERM shutdown is **not** an explicit user boundary — it's a crash artifact, the same category as `agent_close`. The user did not request a new session; the gateway died underneath them. Treating it as terminal (prune + don't recover) is the bug.

## Expected behaviour

Sessions ended with `session_reset` during a non-clean shutdown should be **recoverable** in the same way `agent_close` and `ws_orphan_reap` are: the routing key should be rebuilt on startup, or at minimum the session should remain discoverable via the `/resume` numbered list (which reads from `state.db` via `list_sessions_rich()`, not from `sessions.json`).

## Suggested fixes (ranked)

### Option A — Add `session_reset` to the recovery allowlist (minimal, targeted)

In `hermes_state.py`, `find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer`, extend the end_reason allowlist:

```sql
AND (ended_at IS NULL OR end_reason IN ('agent_close', 'ws_orphan_reap', 'session_reset'))
```

This makes the existing recovery path fire for `session_reset`-ended sessions, so `_prune_stale_sessions_locked()` repoints instead of dropping. Smallest change, addresses the exact symptom.

**Risk:** `session_reset` is also written by `/new` and `/resume` switches (genuine user boundaries). Recovering those would reopen a session the user deliberately left. If this matters, see Option B.

### Option B — Distinguish crash-left `session_reset` from user-initiated `session_reset` (more correct)

Introduce a distinct end_reason for crash-path session resets (e.g. `crash_reset` or `shutdown_reset`), so:
- `_prune_stale_sessions_locked` can tell crash artifacts from explicit user actions
- Recovery can target only the crash variant
- The `/resume` list stays clean of genuinely-abandoned sessions

This is more work but preserves the semantic distinction. The SIGTERM-shutdown path in `gateway/run.py` is the place to emit the new reason.

### Option C — Don't prune routing keys for sessions whose transcripts are still in state.db (defensive)

`_prune_stale_sessions_locked` currently treats `end_reason IS NOT NULL` as "prune". A more defensive rule: only prune when the session is *also* absent from `state.db` (truly gone) or explicitly user-ended (`/new`, `/resume` switch, compression split). Crash artifacts with intact transcripts should keep their routing key so the conversation stays reachable.

## Workaround for affected users

Until a fix lands, sessions can still be resumed by explicit ID:
```
/resume 20260724_080825_862c1807
```
or
```
hermes --resume 20260724_080825_862c1807
```

Find IDs with `hermes sessions list` or `hermes sessions browse`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest `main` (source install at `/home/hermes/hermes-agent`)
- Platform: Telegram (primary symptom), likely affects all gateway platforms
- OS: Linux (Debian 13, kernel 6.12), gateway under `systemd --user` with `Restart=on-failure`
- DB size: 5.2 GB, ~3000 sessions
- Profiles: 5 (main, ops, copywriter, worker, jarvis)

## Related PRs/issues

- #54138 (merged) — introduced the startup pruning that causes this bug
- #55485 / #54878 (merged) — runtime guards for live-gateway message drops; do not address startup pruning
- #61993 / #68539 (open) — about resurrecting the *wrong* session; different problem

items.body:
### Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop chat composer, **Cmd/Ctrl+Z after paste does not undo the paste**. It starts deleting **pre-paste typed text letter by letter**. The pasted block never becomes an undo unit, so undo is effectively broken for the most common edit path (type → paste → fix).

This is a daily-friction P1 on the primary input surface. Same class as already tracked in #49745 / open PR #49746, but **still broken on current `main`** — filing this so the Desktop regression stays visible and prioritized until a merge lands.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop and focus the chat composer.
2. Type a short prefix (e.g. `Hello `).
3. Copy other text to the clipboard (e.g. `world`).
4. Paste into the composer (Cmd+V / Ctrl+V or Edit → Paste). Composer shows `Hello world`.
5. Press Cmd+Z (Ctrl+Z on Windows/Linux) once.

### Expected Behavior

- First Cmd/Ctrl+Z removes **only** the paste → back to `Hello `.
- Further Cmd/Ctrl+Z walks pre-paste keystrokes normally.
- Matches every other chat app / native text field.

### Actual Behavior

- First Cmd/Ctrl+Z does **not** remove the paste.
- Undo instead deletes earlier typed characters **one by one** (e.g. space, then `o`, then `l`…).
- The paste itself is never on the undo stack — you cannot revert it with Cmd/Ctrl+Z.

### Affected Component

- Other (Hermes Desktop Electron renderer — chat composer)
- Path: `apps/desktop/` composer `contentEditable`
- Suggested labels: `type/bug`, `comp/desktop`, `P1` (not TUI)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```
N/A — pure renderer/UI keyboard behavior in the Desktop composer. No gateway/agent runtime state. hermes debug share will not capture this.
```

### Operating System

macOS — Hermes Desktop (same Chromium contentEditable path on Windows/Linux Desktop)

### Python Version

N/A (renderer TS/JS)

### Hermes Version

Desktop current `main` (composer paste path still uses direct DOM insert; see RCA)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

N/A — no exception; DOM mutation succeeds, undo manager never records the paste.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Custom paste path bypasses Blink’s editing pipeline, so contentEditable’s undo manager never gets an entry.

| What | File | Symbol / detail |
|------|------|-----------------|
| Paste handler | `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx` | `handlePaste` — `preventDefault()` then direct insert |
| Direct DOM insert | `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/rich-editor.ts` | `insertPlainTextAtCaret` — `range.deleteContents()` + `range.insertNode(fragment)` |
| Why undo breaks | Chromium / Blink | Undo only records native keystrokes, native paste, and `document.execCommand('insertText')` — not raw `insertNode` |
| Origin | PR #45812 | Large-paste perf: avoid O(n²) `Editor::InsertText` on huge multiline blobs; undo side effect unflagged |
| Prior report + fix PR | #49745, #49746 | Threshold helper `pastePlainTextIntoEditor` (small → execCommand; large → bypass) — **PR still open / unmerged**; main still on broken path |

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx — handlePaste (current main)
event.preventDefault()
insertPlainTextAtCaret(event.currentTarget, pastedText)
scheduleFlushEditorToDraft(event.currentTarget)
```

A synthesized `InputEvent` after `insertNode` does **not** create an undo entry — only the real editing pipeline does.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Same shape as #49746 — land or re-implement:

1. Add `pastePlainTextIntoEditor` in `rich-editor.ts`.
2. **Focused + text length ≤ ~4096:** `document.execCommand('insertText', false, text)` → undo entry.
3. **Unfocused or oversized:** keep `insertPlainTextAtCaret` (safe selection + large-paste perf).
4. Point `handlePaste` at the helper.
5. Unit tests for focused-small / unfocused / oversized branches.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Type → paste → one Cmd/Ctrl+Z removes **only** the paste.
- [ ] Further undo walks pre-paste keystrokes.
- [ ] Large multiline paste (~50KB) does not multi-second freeze the UI.
- [ ] Tests cover the three paste branches.
- [ ] Close as duplicate of #49745 only **after** the fix is on main and verified — until then this is an active Desktop P1.

### Priority

**P1** — core text editing broken on every paste in the primary chat input.
