### Description

On Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (and current main as of 2026-07-26), `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` is correctly detected by `hermes doctor` (“persona configured”), but its content is **never injected** into the system prompt when using a local/custom Ollama endpoint.

The same SOUL.md loads correctly and is used by the model when switching to a cloud provider (OpenRouter).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) + latest main (updated 2026-07-26)
- Install method: git
- OS: Ubuntu / Raspberry Pi 5 (aarch64)
- Provider that fails: custom / local Ollama (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`)
- Model tested: `llama3.2:3b` (also tested `llama3.2:1b`)
- Provider that works: OpenRouter (free model `poolside/laguna-m.1:free`)

### Evidence

**1. File is present and correct**
$ ls -l ~/.hermes/SOUL.md
-rw-rw-r-- 1 gt-hermes gt-hermes 2519 Jul 25 18:29 /home/gt-hermes/.hermes/SOUL.md

**2. Doctor recognizes it**
✓ ~/.hermes/SOUL.md exists (persona configured)

**3. `hermes prompt-size` shows zero identity content (local Ollama)**

<output>
Prompt-size breakdown (platform=cli, model=llama3.2:3b)
System prompt total :   15,235 B  (14.9 KB)
Major blocks:
skills index       :      333 B  (0.3 KB)
memory             :        0 B  (0.0 KB)
user profile       :        0 B  (0.0 KB)
Prompt tiers:
stable (identity/guidance/skills)   :   15,157 B
context (AGENTS.md/cwd files)       :        0 B
volatile (memory/profile/timestamp) :       76 B


**4. Agent itself confirms SOUL.md is missing**

When asked “List every file that was loaded into your system prompt… Do you have a SOUL.md?” the local model replies that there is no SOUL.md in its context.

**5. Cloud provider contrast**

Switching to OpenRouter with the identical SOUL.md causes the agent to correctly adopt the Withnail identity on the first turn.

### Expected behavior

SOUL.md content should appear in the system prompt (and be reflected in `hermes prompt-size`) for local/custom Ollama endpoints the same way it does for cloud providers.

### Actual behavior

SOUL.md is detected by the loader / doctor but dropped before the prompt is assembled when the provider is a local Ollama endpoint.

### Additional notes

- Skills were reduced to a minimal set (skills index ≈ 0.3 KB) — problem still present.
- Sessions were cleared (`rm -rf ~/.hermes/sessions/*`) before each test.
- Problem reproduces consistently on both CLI and after gateway restart.
- Multiple related issues already exist around custom Ollama providers and SOUL.md injection; this appears to be the same class of bug still present on current main.

Happy to provide more logs or run additional diagnostics.

items.title: Desktop: Audio/video playback fails in remote-gateway mode (shows only Download button)

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the Desktop app is connected to a **remote** Hermes gateway (e.g. Mac desktop client connected to a Hermes server running on another machine on the LAN), audio files generated via `text_to_speech` (and presumably other MEDIA:-tagged audio/video attachments) fail to play inline in the chat. The inline player shows no waveform/duration and only offers a 'Download' fallback button — clicking the play control does nothing.

## Root Cause (found while investigating)

In `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx`, the `mediaSrc()` helper unconditionally routes audio/video through the local Electron custom-protocol stream handler, without checking remote-gateway mode first:

```ts
async function mediaSrc(path: string): Promise<string> {
  if (window.hermesDesktop && ['audio', 'video'].includes(mediaKind(path))) {
    return mediaStreamUrl(path)   // <-- always local stream, no isRemoteGateway() check
  }
  return resolveMediaDisplaySrc(path)
}
```

`mediaStreamUrl()` builds a `hermes-media://stream/<path>` URL that is handled entirely inside the local Electron process (`electron/main.ts`, `registerMediaProtocol()`), reading the file directly off the **local** filesystem. When Desktop is in remote mode, the referenced path (e.g. `/data/hermes/cache/audio/tts_....mp3`) only exists on the **gateway/server** machine, not on the client running Desktop — so the local read 404s ('Media not found') and the UI falls back to the download-only affordance.

Compare with the equivalent **image** path in `resolveMediaDisplaySrc()` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts`), which correctly branches:

```ts
export async function resolveMediaDisplaySrc(path: string): Promise<string> {
  if (isInlineMediaSrc(path) || !isFileMediaPath(path)) {
    return path
  }
  if (window.hermesDesktop && isRemoteGateway()) {
    return gatewayMediaDataUrl(path)   // fetches over the authenticated gateway API
  }
  ...
}
```

Audio/video never gets this remote-aware branch because `mediaSrc()` intercepts them earlier and always picks the local stream URL.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes` (or the gateway) on machine A (e.g. a Linux server), with a TTS provider configured (any provider — reproduced with ElevenLabs).
2. On machine B (e.g. a macOS laptop), run Hermes Desktop and connect it to machine A's gateway in **remote** mode.
3. In a chat session on Desktop (routed to machine A), trigger `text_to_speech` (or otherwise produce a `MEDIA:<path>.mp3` attachment).
4. Observe the resulting inline audio card in the chat.

## Expected Behavior

The audio (or video) should stream/play inline in the Desktop chat, fetched from the remote gateway via the authenticated API — the same way images already do in remote mode.

## Actual Behavior

The inline audio/video player fails to load (no duration, play button non-functional) and the UI falls back to showing only a 'Download <kind> file' button. The underlying cause is a 404 from the local `hermes-media://` protocol handler, since the file only exists on the remote gateway machine.

## Suggested Fix

In `mediaSrc()` (`markdown-text.tsx`), check `isRemoteGateway()` before routing to `mediaStreamUrl()`. When in remote mode, either:
- Fall back to `resolveMediaDisplaySrc()`/`gatewayMediaDataUrl()` (data-URL, same as images — simplest, but reintroduces the base64 size cap issue `mediaStreamUrl()` was built to avoid for large media), or
- Add a remote-aware, Range-capable streaming path (e.g. an authenticated `/api/files/stream` endpoint proxied similarly to `hermes-media://`) so large audio/video still streams/seeks properly in remote mode.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (Electron), connected to a remote gateway over LAN
- Server: Linux, Hermes CLI/gateway
- Client: macOS, Hermes Desktop
- TTS provider: ElevenLabs (issue is provider-agnostic — root cause is in the media transport layer, not TTS)

items.title: [mnemosyne] hermes-lcm DB not backed up by weekly rsync

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Problem

The weekly Hermes backup cron job runs rsync with `--exclude='plugins/'`, which means the hermes-lcm SQLite database (`~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm/lcm.db`) is never included in the git backup repo.

The plugin source code is trivially recoverable via `git clone`, but the lcm.db runtime database (containing the DAG-based context engine data) is not backed up. If the DB is lost, all compressed/historical context data accumulated by hermes-lcm is gone.

## Fix applied locally

Updated `backup.sh` to explicitly rsync the lcm.db after the main rsync:

```bash
if [ -f "$HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-lcm/lcm.db" ]; then
  rsync -av     "$HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-lcm/lcm.db"     "$BACKUP_DIR/plugins/hermes-lcm/"
fi
```

## Fix needed upstream

The hermes-agent backup script should either:
1. Include hermes-lcm DB in its backup exclusions exception, or
2. Add a post-rsync step to capture runtime DBs from the plugins directory.

Also: the `hermes memory status` command uses a directory-scan heuristic (`_is_memory_provider_dir` in `plugins/memory/__init__.py`) to check for `register_memory_provider` / `MemoryProvider` in top-level `__init__.py`. This doesn't find mnemosyne because its top-level stub has neither string, even though the entry point (hermes_agent.memory_providers) correctly registers the provider. The entry point and directory scan should agree.

## Reproduction
1. Install hermes-lcm to `~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm`
2. Run weekly backup
3. Check backup repo — no lcm.db present

items.title: [Bug]: `hermes skills update` silently replaces skills with same-named ones from a different registry (data loss)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### What happened

`hermes skills update` (no args) reported a clean success:

```
Updated 4 skill(s).
```

In reality it replaced two skills with **same-named skills from a different registry by different authors**, deleting the originals' scripts. The lockfile's `source` was silently rewritten.

| Skill | Before (`clawhub`) | After (`skills.sh`) | Damage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stock-market-pro` | 8 files incl. `scripts/{yf,news,uw,options_links,ddg_search}.py` | **1 file** (`SKILL.md`) | all 5 scripts deleted; the new `SKILL.md` still instructs `uv run --script scripts/yf price [TICKER]` → **self-referentially broken** |
| `reddit` | `scripts/reddit.mjs`, `skill-card.md`, `_meta.json`, `.clawhub/origin.json` | another author's README/SKILL.md | `reddit.mjs` deleted; the install was then blocked mid-flight by the security scanner, leaving a **half-swapped tree** |

The lockfile diff is the diagnostic fingerprint:

```diff
-  "source": "clawhub",              +  "source": "skills.sh",
-  "identifier": "stock-market-pro"  +  "identifier": "skills-sh/sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills/stock-market-pro"
-  "files": [8 entries]              +  "files": ["SKILL.md"]
```

### Why it's hard to notice

`hermes skills check` afterwards reports `up_to_date` — it faithfully tracks the *new* upstream. Nothing in the CLI surfaces that you're now running a different author's code. Only a file-level diff reveals it. Recovery was only cheap because `~/.hermes` happened to be a git repo.

### Root cause

Two independent defects, either of which is sufficient:

**1. `tools/skills_hub.py::check_for_skill_updates`** — the candidate-source list falls back to *every* registry when the recorded source has no adapter:

```python
candidate_sources = [src for src in sources if _source_matches(src, source_name)] or sources
```

Skill names are not namespaced across registries, so a same-named skill elsewhere satisfies `src.fetch(identifier)` and is reported as *this* entry's update.

**2. `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py::do_update`** — passes the identifier to `do_install` with no source constraint:

```python
do_install(entry["identifier"], category=category, force=True, console=c)
```

When the identifier is bare (no slash, e.g. `reddit`), `do_install` sends it through `_resolve_short_name`'s fuzzy catalog search across all sources, which picks a foreign-registry match and installs it.

`reddit` shows both interacting: the resolver picked `theglove44/reddit` from skills.sh, the security scanner then hard-blocked the install (same `export REDDIT_PASSWORD=` false positive as #59010's neighbourhood) — but **files had already been overwritten before the scan gate**, so a blocked install is not atomic.

### Expected behaviour

An update should never change a skill's source registry. A cross-registry move is a *provenance change*, not an update.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)`, macOS 26.5.2 arm64
- Affected skills sourced from `clawhub`, hijacked by `skills.sh`'s `sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills` mirror

### Related

Same `do_update` → `do_install(bare_name)` → `_resolve_short_name` path as the resolver problems in #6866 and #37008, but with a data-destructive outcome rather than a no-op or hang.

I have a fix + regression tests and will open a PR referencing this issue.

items.title: [Bug] v0.19.0 --oneshot exits 0 with a non-challenge response under openai-codex

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

On the official Hermes Agent v0.19.0 image, a public CLI `--oneshot` invocation using the configured `openai-codex` default (`gpt-5.5`) can exit with status 0 while its final stdout does not answer a fresh deterministic challenge.

## Expected

For each invocation, a prompt supplies two fresh opaque values and requires an exact reordered response. A valid final response must contain both values in the requested order.

## Actual

The public process exits 0 and emits bounded UTF-8 plain text, but the final response contains neither fresh value. The response is therefore neither a prompt echo nor a valid completion of the current invocation. No raw model response or credential material was retained.

## Reproduction conditions

- Official v0.19.0 image digest: `sha256:f7b35053268f532f98955195c909f15a230470fbcbdacaa9fdecb95707dad04a`
- Fresh isolated candidate, started through the official gateway entrypoint with private copied config/data and workspace; no host ports or live mounts.
- Temporary egress was attached only for the bounded call and removed during cleanup.
- Public one-shot invocation with `--ignore-rules`; candidate CLI toolsets disabled.
- Configured provider/model default: `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5`.

This was reproduced after the candidate had passed public version/config/auth/gateway checks. 

## Reproduction Steps

Added in comment below.

## Relationship to existing reports

This may be related to #5736 (empty `response.output` from the Codex agent loop) and #7968 (reusing earlier content after an empty post-tool response), but it is not the same observed behavior:

- neither an empty-output diagnostic nor a fallback error was exposed;
- the reproduction is a simple isolated one-shot invocation with candidate CLI toolsets disabled, rather than a multi-turn tool-call workflow; and
- the terminal process reports success but its final response fails a fresh response contract.

## Request

Please confirm whether this is a known v0.19.0 Codex/one-shot regression and advise the smallest supported diagnostic or fix. A minimal deterministic canary is available privately if a maintainer wants a sanitized request/response capture.

items.title: WhatsApp self-chat replies can falsely satisfy group mention gating

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

In WhatsApp `self-chat` mode, replying to an earlier message from the shared self number can be classified as replying to the bot. In groups that require a mention, this makes Hermes respond even though the user only replied to their own message and did not mention the agent.

## Reproduction

1. Run the WhatsApp adapter in the default `self-chat` mode.
2. Enable group access with `require_mention: true`.
3. In a group, reply from the shared self identity to an earlier message authored by that same identity, without an explicit mention.
4. The message passes `_should_process_message` because `quotedParticipant` matches a value in `botIds`.

## Root cause

`_message_is_reply_to_bot` checks the quoted participant against the bot identity set but does not distinguish a self-authored reply in shared-number mode. The sender and quoted participant can both legitimately overlap the bot identity there.

## Expected behavior

A shared-number self-reply should not count as an implicit mention. Explicit mentions must continue to work, and a different participant replying to a bot-authored message must still pass the group gate.

items.title: [Bug]: Output-cap 400 from OpenAI-compatible relays is not parsed for retry

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes receives an OpenAI-compatible provider error like:

```text
API call failed after 3 retries: [400]: max_tokens (98304) exceeds model's maximum output tokens (65536) for model deepseek-v4-flash
```

it treats the error as a generic failure instead of extracting the provider's stated output-token cap and retrying with a safe `max_tokens` value.

This can happen even when Hermes' configured `model.max_tokens` is already at the model output cap (`65536`), because retry/continuation paths or upstream relay translation can produce a larger effective request cap.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes to use an OpenAI-compatible relay/model that reports a separate maximum output-token cap, e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`.
2. Use a long-running session or retry path that results in an oversized effective `max_tokens` request.
3. Observe the provider return a 400 with `max_tokens (...) exceeds model's maximum output tokens (...)`.

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should classify this as an output-cap error, parse the provider's stated cap, and route through the existing retry path that lowers the one-shot output cap instead of hard-failing or treating this as input context overflow.

## Actual Behavior

The existing output-cap parser handles several provider phrasings, but not the `exceeds model's maximum output tokens` wording, so Hermes does not recover from this deterministic provider 400.

## Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

## Debug Report

Not attached. This was reproduced from a local managed Hermes install request dump and verified against current `main` in a clean project checkout.

## Environment

- OS: Debian/trixie-based Linux
- Python: 3.13.5 in the project test venv
- Hermes source: current `main` at `6d1e08b2b`
- Model/provider symptom: `deepseek-v4-flash` via OpenAI-compatible relay

## Root Cause Analysis

`agent/model_metadata.py` already contains `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()` and `is_output_cap_error()` for provider-specific max-token wording, but neither recognizes this common relay wording:

```text
max_tokens (98304) exceeds model's maximum output tokens (65536)
```

Since the cap value is present in the provider error, Hermes can safely parse `65536` and use the existing output-cap retry behavior.

## Proposed Fix

Add parser/classifier support for the `exceeds model's maximum output tokens (...)` form and add focused regression coverage in `tests/test_output_cap_parsing.py`.

## Validation

```text
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_output_cap_parsing.py -q
# 22 passed
```

## PR

A fix branch is prepared at `ekinnee/hermes-agent:agent/deepseek-output-cap-parser`.

items.title: [Bug]: hermes sessions recover source-fingerprint error doesn't enumerate that the parent CLI session counts as a 'Hermes process'

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug: `hermes sessions recover` source-fingerprint error doesn't enumerate that the parent CLI session counts

### Summary

When `hermes sessions recover` is run from inside an interactive CLI session (i.e. `hermes` is already running and you invoke `recover` from that same process group), the source-fingerprint check fails with:

> The source database bundle changed while it was being copied. Stop every Hermes process using this profile and retry.

The error message tells the user to "Stop every Hermes process" — but a user reading this will think of the gateway, a different shell, a cron daemon, etc. They will not realize that **the parent hermes CLI session itself is a "Hermes process using this profile"** that writes session bookkeeping (compression tick, LCM, context-tracking) to state.db on a background thread. Stopping the gateway is necessary but not sufficient; the only way to make the tool happy with the live source is to either kill the parent CLI or feed `--source` an immutable snapshot.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Hermes CLI session (`hermes` in your terminal) with an open conversation
2. Stop the gateway: `hermes gateway stop`
3. From the same terminal (still inside the active CLI), run: `hermes sessions recover --source ~/.hermes/state.db --output /tmp/recovered.db`
4. Observe: the tool fails after the first copy attempt with "The source database bundle changed while it was being copied."

### Expected Behavior

Either:
- The error message enumerates the parent CLI session as one of the "Hermes processes" to stop, **with** a specific suggestion to invoke recover from a fresh shell, or
- The tool offers a `--self-snapshot` flag that takes the source snapshot via `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` API (which is concurrent-writer safe) before doing the fingerprint check, so the parent CLI's background writes don't cause the failure.

### Actual Behavior

The error message is technically correct ("the source database bundle changed") but practically misleading. The user has stopped the only process they can see (the gateway), runs the command again, and it fails again — because the parent CLI's own background writes still hit the DB. There is no hint in the message that "your own shell is the problem."

The only work-around I found: take a stable snapshot of `state.db` myself using the SQLite backup API, then point `--source` at the snapshot file:

```python
import sqlite3
src = sqlite3.connect('/home/hermes-pi/.hermes/state.db')
dst = sqlite3.connect('/home/hermes-pi/.hermes/state-snapshot/state.db')
with dst:
    src.backup(dst)
```

Then `hermes sessions recover --source <snapshot> --output <new> --work-dir <dir>` succeeds. This is documented in the recovery procedure at `wiki/audits/hermes-state-db-recovery-2026-07-27` and a skill at `~/.hermes/skills/devops/hermes-state-db-recovery/`.

### Affected Component

- [x] Sessions (CLI: `hermes sessions recover`, `hermes sessions repair`)

### Root Cause Analysis

`hermes_cli/session_recovery.py`'s `_copy_source_bundle()` correctly uses `offline_file_access()` (commits `9657f6e34` + `a1c4d9995`) to hold the connection-lifecycle lock during the raw copy, preventing NEW connections from opening mid-copy. The outer safety net is the source-fingerprint check (`_source_fingerprint(source) == inspection["source_fingerprint"]`) in `_snapshot_and_inspect()` at line ~324, which compares file mtime/size before vs. after the copy.

The fingerprint check is **correct** — it catches a real race (a connection that was already open before the lock was acquired, or a writer that gets through the lock). But:

1. The error message at line 333-337 says "Stop every Hermes process using this profile" without enumerating that the **parent CLI session** is one of those processes.
2. The fingerprint check is the only thing standing between the user and a usable tool — there's no automatic "take a snapshot, then check" pre-step.

The fix for #1 is a one-line docstring change. The fix for #2 is a `--self-snapshot` (or similar) flag that calls `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` first, then runs the existing logic on the snapshot. The backup API is concurrent-writer-safe and would make the tool just work for the most common case (running from a parent CLI).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (commit `0054c7edc`, local fork of `ether-btc/hermes-agent` synced to upstream)
- Python 3.11.15 in the hermes-agent venv
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), aarch64
- state.db: 3.17 GB, page-level corruption (separate incident, see [post-mortem](https://github.com/ether-btc/wiki/blob/master/audits/hermes-state-db-recovery-2026-07-27.md))

### Suggested Fix

Option A (minimal, doc-only): update the error message in `hermes_cli/session_recovery.py` ~line 334:

```python
raise SessionRecoverySafetyError(
    "The source database bundle changed while it was being copied. "
    "This includes background writes from the parent `hermes` CLI session "
    "that issued this command — the simplest workaround is to invoke "
    "`hermes sessions recover` from a fresh shell, or to point `--source` "
    "at a stable SQLite backup-API snapshot of the database."
)
```

Option B (behavior change): add a `--self-snapshot` flag (default off for backwards-compat) that:

1. Calls `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` to take a stable snapshot of the source into the work-dir
2. Continues the existing logic on the snapshot file
3. Skips the fingerprint check (since the snapshot is by definition stable)

Happy to send either as a PR from my fork.

### Work-around Procedure (for users who hit this now)

```bash
# 1. Stop the gateway
hermes gateway stop

# 2. Take a stable SQLite backup-API snapshot
python3 -c "
import sqlite3
src = sqlite3.connect('/home/hermes/state.db')
dst = sqlite3.connect('/home/hermes/state-snapshot/state.db')
with dst: src.backup(dst)
"

# 3. Run recover against the snapshot
mkdir -p ~/.hermes/recovery-workdir
hermes sessions recover \
    --source ~/.hermes/state-snapshot/state.db \
    --output ~/.hermes/recovered-state.db \
    --work-dir ~/.hermes/recovery-workdir
```

This worked on my 3.17 GB state.db in ~8 minutes. The recovered DB was 1.3 GB (the tool rebuilt a clean v23 FTS index from scratch), FTS verified, `hermes sessions repair --check-only` and `hermes sessions optimize-storage --yes` both pass.

### Debug Report

Not uploaded — this is a UX/documentation issue, not a runtime crash. The full procedure and work-around is in the post-mortem linked above.

items.title: Cron job delivery UI: change dropdown to checkboxes (allow multi-select)

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Problem

In the Hermes Web UI cron management page, the **delivery method (deliver)** field is a single-select dropdown — users can only pick one option (e.g. "local" OR "origin"), never both.

## User Need

Users sometimes want to **both save cron results locally (local) AND push them to chat (origin)** at the same time. The backend API already supports comma-joined values like `"origin,local"`, but the frontend dropdown restricts this.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the single-select dropdown (`<select>`) with a **checkbox group** (`<input type="checkbox">`):

- ☐ Push to chat (origin)
- ☐ Save to local (local)

Users can check 1 or both options. On submit, the checked values are joined with a comma into the backend format.

## Technical Context

The `cronjob` tool's `deliver` parameter already supports comma-joined values, e.g. `"origin,local"`.

## Relevant Files

- `cron/jobs.json` — the `"deliver"` field stores the value

items.title: [Bug]: Discord adapter allow/deny gates are process-global, breaking per-profile isolation under multiplex_profiles

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
### Bug Description


  Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, multiple Discord profiles each with their own bot token and their own `discord.allowed_channels` cannot
  keep their channel gates isolated. All Discord adapters in the process share a single `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` environment variable, written
  first-writer-wins at config load and read via `os.getenv` on the inbound message path.

  The practical result: **the first Discord profile to initialize pins the allowed-channel list for every other Discord profile in the process.** Every
  later profile silently ignores all messages in its own channel. There is no error, no warning, and no log line above DEBUG.

  The same applies to `discord.ignored_channels`, `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`, and `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` — so this is an authorization isolation gap, not
  only a routing one: every muxed Discord profile enforces the *first* profile's user/role allowlist.

  This breaks at two profiles. It is not a scale issue.

  ## Environment

  - Hermes Agent `v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)`
  - Git install, commit `893dcda70`
  - Linux, per-user systemd gateway units
  - `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` on a dedicated multiplex `HERMES_HOME` whose `profiles/` contains only the intended served profiles
  - Two Discord profiles, **distinct bot tokens**, **distinct** `discord.allowed_channels`

  Sanitized configuration:

  ```yaml
  # <mux-home>/config.yaml
  gateway:
    multiplex_profiles: true

  # <mux-home>/profiles/profile-a/config.yaml
  discord:
    allowed_channels: "<channel-A>"
    require_mention: false

  # <mux-home>/profiles/profile-b/config.yaml
  discord:
    allowed_channels: "<channel-B>"
    require_mention: false
  ```

  Each profile supplies its own `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` in its own `.env`. Startup reports no duplicate-token conflict, and both adapters connect
  successfully.


### Steps to Reproduce


  ## Reproduction

  1. Start the multiplexed gateway with the configuration above. Both bots connect; the log shows `Connected as A#nnnn` then `Connected as B#nnnn`.
  2. Send a normal message in `<channel-A>` (profile A's channel). It is answered correctly by profile A.
  3. Send a normal message in `<channel-B>` (profile B's channel). **Nothing happens.** No session is created, no inbound event is recorded, no error
  is logged.
  4. Restart the gateway so that profile B initializes first (`Connected as B#nnnn` before `Connected as A#nnnn`).
  5. Repeat steps 2-3. The behavior inverts exactly: profile B now works and profile A is silent.

  The winner is determined solely by adapter initialization order, which confirms process-global state rather than per-profile config.

  I reproduced this twice with different profile pairs; in both cases the profile that initialized second was the one that went silent.


### Expected Behavior


  ## Expected behavior

  Each Discord adapter enforces the `discord.allowed_channels` (and `ignored_channels` / `allowed_users` / `allowed_roles`) of the profile it serves,
  exactly as it would in a single-profile gateway. Per the multi-profile gateway docs, unique bot tokens are the only stated precondition for polling
  platforms under multiplexing.

### Actual Behavior


  ## Actual behavior

  All Discord adapters in the process enforce whichever profile happened to load its config first.

  ## Code-level evidence

  Line numbers are from `v0.19.0`; the same code is present on `main` at the time of writing.

  **1. Config is bridged into process-global env, first-writer-wins** — `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:9421-9425`:

  ```python
  ac = discord_cfg.get("allowed_channels")
  if ac is not None and not os.getenv("DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS"):
      if isinstance(ac, list):
          ac = ",".join(str(v) for v in ac)
      os.environ["DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS"] = str(ac)
  ```

  `_apply_yaml_config` runs once per profile config load. After the first profile writes, the `not os.getenv(...)` guard makes every subsequent
  profile's write a no-op. The same guard is used for ~20 bridged `DISCORD_*` variables.

  **2. The inbound gate reads that global, not per-adapter config** — `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:7167-7172`:

  ```python
  allowed_channels_raw = os.getenv("DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS", "")
  if allowed_channels_raw:
      allowed_channels = {ch.strip() for ch in allowed_channels_raw.split(",") if ch.strip()}
      if "*" not in allowed_channels and not (channel_keys & allowed_channels):
          logger.debug("[%s] Ignoring message in non-allowed channel: %s", self.name, channel_keys)
          return False
  ```

  There is no `self.config.extra.get("allowed_channels")` read anywhere in the adapter. The rejection happens inside the adapter on the discord.py
  event callback, before any gateway event is emitted — so no gateway hook can observe or correct it.

  Further `os.getenv("DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS")` reads at lines 1984, 4131, 4275, and 4358 (slash-command authorization) share the same problem.

  **3. User/role allowlists are snapshotted at connect from the same global** — `adapter.py:1125-1139`:

  ```python
  allowed_env = os.getenv("DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS", "")
  if allowed_env:
      self._allowed_user_ids = {...}
  roles_env = os.getenv("DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES", "")
  if roles_env:
      self._allowed_role_ids = {...}
  ```

  **4. The per-profile runtime scope cannot help here** — `gateway/run.py:1706-1721` states explicitly:

  > `set_secret_scope` — installs the profile's `.env` secrets as the authoritative credential source, so `get_secret` reads this profile's keys and
  never the process-global `os.environ` (which in a multiplexer may hold another profile's values). … Loading the profile's `.env` here does **not** 
  mutate `os.environ`.

  So the codebase already recognizes this exact hazard and solves it for credentials — but the adapter's gates bypass that seam by calling `os.getenv`
  directly.

  **5. The correct per-adapter pattern already exists in the same file** — `adapter.py:5757-5759`, for a sibling setting:

  ```python
  raw = self.config.extra.get("free_response_channels")
  if raw is None:
      raw = os.getenv("DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS", "")
  ```

  `require_mention`, `thread_require_mention`, `history_backfill`, and others already read `self.config.extra` with an env fallback. The allow/deny
  gates are the settings that were not migrated. This looks like an oversight rather than a deliberate design constraint — the `_apply_yaml_config`
  docstring notes the env bridge was kept to avoid rewriting call sites, while `PlatformConfig.extra` is described as "the per-adapter source of truth
  … which keeps multiplexed profiles isolated."


### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://dpaste.com/CAVZFWBXV
  agent.log    https://dpaste.com/ABYLKSXVN
  gateway.log  https://dpaste.com/7YRQWLDMB
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)


  ## Suggested fix

  1. In the Discord adapter, read `allowed_channels`, `ignored_channels`, `allowed_users`, and `allowed_roles` from `self.config.extra` first, falling
  back to `os.getenv` — matching the existing `free_response_channels` pattern. Seed those keys in `_apply_yaml_config`'s returned `extra` dict.
  2. Resolve `allowed_users` / `allowed_roles` per message rather than snapshotting at `connect()`, or snapshot from per-adapter config.
  3. For the `.env`-supplied form of these variables, read through the routed profile's secret scope rather than `os.getenv` — the approach proposed in
  #61985 (`_profile_scope_for` plus a scope-aware `_getenv`).
  4. Add regression coverage: two profiles under `multiplex_profiles` with distinct `allowed_channels`, asserting each adapter accepts only its own
  channel, in both initialization orders.
  5. Consider a startup warning when `multiplex_profiles` is on and two served profiles configure conflicting values for any env-bridged gate.

  ## Related

  - #61985 — "fix(gateway): scope authz allowlist reads to the routed profile" identified the identical root cause for `*_ALLOWED_USERS` at the gateway
  authz layer and proposed the scope-aware `_getenv` approach. It was closed unmerged on 2026-07-16. This report concerns the same class of bug one
  layer lower, inside the platform adapter, where the channel gate also lives.
  - #57417 — per-profile credential isolation (fixed); this is the analogous gap for gate/allowlist configuration.
  - #69178 — native Discord `/model` and `/profile` ignore multiplexed channel `profile_routes`. Different mechanism (one shared token + routes), but
  adjacent: both are per-profile resolution gaps on the Discord path under multiplexing.

  ## Documentation note

  `docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways` states that polling platforms "work fine multiplexed" and names unique bot tokens per profile as the only
  precondition. It does not mention that channel and user gates are shared process-wide. Until this is fixed, that section may warrant a caveat — the
  current behavior silently drops inbound messages rather than failing fast the way a duplicate token does.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Feature]: Implement a default plugin for no API key web_extract functionality

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

All built-in web_extract providers either use a cloud provider with an API key, or if local functionality is available, requires self-hosting an entire professional web crawling server in Docker. Meanwhile, `ddgs` exists for web_search, and works free with no API key or setup.

### Proposed Solution

Provide the option to use a free cloud provider that doesn't require an API key, or signing up for an account.

And/or, provide the option to use a lightweight, no config, local HTML to markdown converter.

The downside with a lightweight local provider is that without running an entire browser through Playwright or something, it will usually be only capable of rendering static html without running javascript. *However*, the good side of this is that it greatly reduces surface area.

At least one free cloud provider exists currently: [Jina](https://jina.ai), which provides a limited amount of free requests for searching and extracting. It's possible to get a trial API key without signing up or logging in, though, to get some free trial credits and then pay for more.

As for local scrapers, there are several options, and there have been issues and pull requests around specific solutions, which I'll try to mention here in this one issue to try to centralize the discussion a bit:

#65179
#65228
#50456
#37187
#68516

And possibly many others listed

To me, the most promising options appear to be Trafilatura, Markitdown, or something like html2text. Trafilatura has built-in cruft filtering, but others might be combined by first processing the HTML through the Readability function to filter out ads and stuff.

[Crawl4AI](https://github.com/unclecode/crawl4ai) also looks like a promising local web scraper, it's not lightweight but it seems to be pretty popular, and possibly doesn't require an entire Docker server to run, but might require some setup.



### Alternatives Considered

Just write third party plugins for different providers

Or teach your agent how to run trafilatura or Markitdown with curl.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Description

`video_analyze` ignores the configured auxiliary vision model and sends the video payload to the **main model** instead, even when:
- `model.supports_vision: false` is explicitly set
- `auxiliary.vision.provider` is set to a provider (e.g., `anthropic`) that natively supports video blocks
- The main model (e.g., DeepSeek V4) rejects video blocks with HTTP 400

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure:
```
auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-haiku-4-5
```
And set `model.supports_vision: false`.

2. Call `video_analyze(video_url='/path/to/video.mpg', question='Describe')`

3. Observe HTTP 400

## Actual Behavior

Returns:
```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[0].content: unknown variant `video`, expected one of `text`, `image`, `document`, `tool_reference`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `web_search_tool_result`, `thinking`...'}}
```

The request was sent to DeepSeek (main model), not Anthropic (aux vision). Anthropic natively accepts `video` content blocks -- confirmed working via direct API calls.

`vision_analyze` (for images) also failed with `[Unsupported Image]` due to the same routing issue, despite ANTHROPIC_API_KEY being valid and verified via direct calls.

## Expected Behavior

`video_analyze` should route to the auxiliary vision provider when `model.supports_vision: false`. If that provider supports video natively (e.g., Anthropic), it should work directly. Otherwise, fall back to frame extraction.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: Homebrew (recent)
- Python: 3.14.6
- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- Main model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (supports_vision: false)
- Auxiliary vision: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY resolved from macOS Keychain, verified working

## Related

- #70948 -- vision_analyze fails to fall back to aux model when main model lacks vision (images only, fix committed 2h ago)
- #72275 -- video_analyze sends raw video base64 that most providers reject with 400 (wire format, distinct from routing)

items.title: RFC: define separate contracts for profile cloning and backup/restore

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes currently has two different lifecycle operations with overlapping copy/exclusion policy:

- Profile cloning is implemented in `hermes_cli/profiles.py` (`create_profile`, `--clone`, `--clone-all`, profile export/import).
- Backup, quick snapshots, restore, and import are implemented in `hermes_cli/backup.py`.
- The dashboard profile-create endpoint in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` translates UI flags into the clone modes.

The distinction is not explicit enough. A clone should create a **new, independent profile identity**. A backup should create a **recoverable point-in-time artifact** for an existing Hermes home/profile, with a restore path. Today `--clone-all`, export/import, exclusion lists, credentials, history, snapshots, and runtime-state handling overlap and can drift.

## Decision required

Write and approve a short architecture decision covering:

1. Definitions and invariants for **clone**, **backup**, **restore**, **profile export/import**, and **quick snapshot**.
2. Ownership boundaries between the clone domain and backup/restore domain.
3. Data classification matrix: identity/persona, config, secrets, skills/plugins, memories, sessions, cron, runtime state, caches, nested backups, external-provider state.
4. Whether `--clone-all` remains as a compatibility alias, is renamed, or is deprecated.
5. Whether profile export/import is distribution/portability or disaster recovery, and therefore which domain owns it.
6. Compatibility expectations for CLI, dashboard/desktop API, existing archives, Docker/custom `HERMES_HOME`, and named profiles.
7. Shared low-level primitives that are allowed without coupling the two domain workflows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision document defines the operations in user language and code-level invariants.
- [ ] Every profile artifact category has an explicit clone/backup/restore policy.
- [ ] Secret and runtime-state behavior is explicit and defaults safe.
- [ ] Backward-compatibility and deprecation strategy is approved.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation issues can be accepted without reopening core semantics.

## Likely code/docs touched

- `hermes_cli/profiles.py`
- `hermes_cli/backup.py`
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/profile.py`
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/backup.py`
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py`
- `website/docs/`

items.body:
## Goal

Move profile duplication behind one explicit clone-domain API whose only responsibility is creating a new, independent profile from a source profile according to a declared clone policy.

## Current seam

`hermes_cli/profiles.py::create_profile()` currently owns fresh creation, selective clone, full-tree clone, exclusion policy, runtime stripping, config migration, skill seeding, persona/memory copying, and alias creation. `_CLONE_*` policy is interleaved with profile export policy and backup-like concerns.

## Scope

- Introduce a focused clone service/policy module (exact module name to follow the RFC).
- Represent clone modes with explicit typed policy/options rather than interacting booleans (`clone_from`, `clone_all`, `clone_config`).
- Keep orchestration in profile creation, but move clone inventory/copy/strip/validation behavior out of the general profile CRUD module.
- Produce a structured clone result/manifest suitable for CLI and API reporting.
- Guarantee destination cleanup/rollback when cloning fails partway through.
- Keep backup archives, quick snapshots, restore logic, and backup retention out of the clone domain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clone creates a new profile identity and never mutates the source.
- [ ] Clone inclusion/exclusion behavior follows the approved artifact matrix.
- [ ] Partial failures do not leave a profile that appears valid.
- [ ] Source and destination path/symlink safety is covered.
- [ ] `create_profile()` delegates rather than carrying clone internals.
- [ ] Existing supported clone behavior remains compatible or emits the approved deprecation path.
- [ ] Focused tests cover default and named sources, Docker/custom homes, secrets, history exclusion, symlinks, and failure rollback.

## Likely files

- `hermes_cli/profiles.py`
- New focused module under `hermes_cli/`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py`
- New focused clone tests under `tests/hermes_cli/`

## Dependency

Blocked by the clone/backup contract RFC.

## Goal

Make backup/restore a standalone recovery domain with no dependency on profile-clone behavior or clone-specific exclusion lists.

## Current seam

`hermes_cli/backup.py` currently combines full zip backup/import, SQLite-safe copying and integrity checks, external memory-provider paths, quick snapshots, pruning, and targeted safety restoration. Profile export/import and clone-all carry partially overlapping portability and exclusion semantics elsewhere.

## Scope

- Define a recovery-domain API for backup creation, inspection, restore/import, and quick snapshots.
- Make target scope explicit: active profile, named profile, or full Hermes installation (including the policy for nested profiles).
- Add archive metadata/versioning and a machine-readable manifest describing source scope and included categories.
- Centralize restore safety: path traversal, symlinks, runtime-state filtering, secret permissions, SQLite consistency/integrity, collision handling, and rollback/failure behavior.
- Keep new-profile identity creation and clone policy out of this domain.
- Preserve import support for existing backup artifacts according to the RFC compatibility decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Backup artifacts identify format version, source scope, and contents.
- [ ] Restore validates an archive before mutating the target.
- [ ] Restore has an explicit overwrite/collision policy and does not revive foreign runtime state.
- [ ] SQLite and external-provider state remain consistent and testable.
- [ ] Backup retention/nesting behavior is explicit.
- [ ] Recovery APIs do not import or invoke clone-domain orchestration.
- [ ] Existing backup/import and snapshot tests are reorganized around the new boundary and remain green.

## Likely files

- `hermes_cli/backup.py`
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/backup.py`
- New focused recovery modules under `hermes_cli/`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_backup.py`

## Dependency

Blocked by the clone/backup contract RFC.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Objective

Reorganize Hermes profile lifecycle code so **cloning** and **backup/restore** are separate user journeys, domain APIs, and implementation boundaries.

- **Clone:** create a new, independent profile identity from a source profile under an explicit copy policy.
- **Backup/restore:** capture and recover point-in-time state for an existing Hermes home/profile with archive validation and restore safety.

The implementation may share narrowly scoped filesystem/archive primitives, but clone orchestration must not behave like disaster recovery, and recovery orchestration must not create profile identities.

## Why this needs an initiative

The current behavior spans `hermes_cli/profiles.py`, `hermes_cli/backup.py`, both CLI parser surfaces, `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, dashboard/desktop profile creation, credentials/history/runtime-state rules, SQLite consistency, old archive compatibility, and cross-platform filesystem behavior. Splitting it without a tracked contract would invite semantic drift or data loss.

## Delivery sequence

### Phase 1 — Decide the boundary
- [x] #72376

### Phase 2 — Establish domain ownership (parallel after RFC)
- [x] #72377
- [x] #72378
- [ ] #72381 (scaffold matrix and invariants)

### Phase 3 — Migrate user surfaces
- [x] #72379
- [x] #72380

### Phase 4 — Prove and communicate
- [ ] #72381 (complete E2E gate)
- [x] #72382

## Initiative acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clone and backup/restore have approved, non-overlapping contracts.
- [ ] Domain orchestration is separated in code, with only intentional low-level helpers shared.
- [ ] CLI and dashboard/desktop use the same terminology and policy model.
- [ ] Existing users and archives follow a tested compatibility/deprecation path.
- [ ] Security/data-loss invariants pass against real temporary homes and SQLite files.
- [ ] Documentation provides a clear “clone or backup?” decision guide.

## Out of scope

- Reworking profile distribution install/update unless the RFC finds a direct contract conflict.
- Adding cloud backup providers.
- Changing unrelated session recovery or checkpoint behavior.

items.title: Desktop on Windows: WebSocket ready race under GIL stall — ready_send_failed / reconnect loop

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
# Desktop on Windows: WebSocket ready race under GIL stall — `ready_send_failed` / reconnect loop

**Labels (suggested):** `bug`, `desktop`, `windows`, `tui-gateway`  
**Platform:** Windows 10/11 (build 26100)  
**Affected:** Hermes Desktop (Electron) + `hermes serve` / `tui_gateway`  
**Approx. version:** v0.19.0 (commits around `eb527605` / `136f8dab`)

---

## Summary / 摘要

On Windows, Hermes Desktop often fails to reach a usable state: the window opens, but the UI stays in **connecting / couldn't start / reset**. Logs show the backend event loop stalling for ~8–20s (sometimes ~37s) under GIL pressure during cold start; the renderer WebSocket times out waiting for `gateway.ready`, disconnects, and the server then fails with `ready_send_failed` — triggering a Desktop bootstrap reset loop.

Windows 上 Hermes Desktop 窗口能起来，但经常进不了可用状态（connecting / couldn't start / reset）。冷启动时事件循环因 GIL 压力卡顿约 8–20s（偶发 ~37s）；客户端等待 `gateway.ready` 超时断开，服务端 accept 后再发 ready 已晚，形成 `ready_send_failed` → Desktop reset 循环。

---

## Environment / 环境

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| OS | Windows 10/11, build **26100** |
| Install | git install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent` |
| Desktop | Electron unpacked: `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked\Hermes.exe` |
| Python | 3.11.15 (venv) |
| Backend | `hermes serve` with `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` |
| Approx. version | ~v0.19.0 (`eb527605` / `136f8dab` era) |

---

## Steps to reproduce / 复现步骤

1. Install Hermes Agent via git under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent` (venv Python 3.11).
2. Launch Desktop from the unpacked Electron build (`Hermes.exe`).
3. Observe cold start (especially with Windows Defender real-time scanning enabled, no exclusion for `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`).
4. Repeat open/close or wait for bootstrap reset cycles.

> Tip: Defender scanning of the hermes tree strongly amplifies GIL stalls on first import/warm-up.

---

## Expected behavior / 期望行为

- Desktop connects to the local TUI gateway WebSocket.
- Server accepts the connection and successfully sends `gateway.ready` **before** the client timeout.
- UI reaches a usable ready state without a reconnect/reset loop.

---

## Actual behavior / 实际行为

- Window appears, but UI frequently never becomes usable.
- User-facing: “can't open” / stuck connecting / “couldn't start” / repeated reset.
- Server accepts WS, then fails to send the ready frame because the client already disconnected during the stall.
- Desktop bootstrap logs show reset + “Restarting desktop connection” loops.

---

## Logs / 日志特征

### `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\gui.log`

```text
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled NN.Ns (GIL pressure suspected)
INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:XXXXX
WARNING/ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws send failed ... WebSocketDisconnect
ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws ready frame send failed ...
INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws closed ... reason=ready_send_failed
```

Typical stall duration: **~8–20s**, occasionally **~37s**. Client disconnects during the stall; by the time the server tries to send `gateway.ready`, the peer is gone.

### Desktop log (`desktop.log`)

```text
[boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
[bootstrap] reset requested by renderer; clearing latched failure
[boot] Restarting desktop connection
```

---

## Not the root cause (please ignore) / 误报说明

The following message appears in logs but is **expected** for headless `hermes serve` and should **not** be treated as the root cause:

```text
could not read served dashboard token ... 404
Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled
```

This is normal when the dashboard / web UI is disabled under Desktop’s headless backend.

---

## Suspected cause / 根因分析

1. **Warm-up vs accept race**  
   After Desktop spawns `hermes serve`, lifespan starts executor warm-up of modules such as `hermes_cli.gateway` (e.g. `_warm_gateway_module`), but **older code accepts WebSocket connections before warm-up finishes**.

2. **Windows cold-start + Defender → GIL pressure**  
   Cold import / compile + Defender real-time scanning causes multi-second event-loop stalls (`event loop stalled … GIL pressure suspected`).

3. **Ready timeout → disconnect → `ready_send_failed`**  
   Renderer waits for `gateway.ready`; during the stall it times out and disconnects. Server accepts late, fails to send ready (`ready_send_failed`), Desktop bootstrap resets and reconnects → loop.

4. **Extra startup contention**  
   Desktop cron ticker / plugin mount / MCP discovery and similar work during the startup window also compete for the GIL and worsen stalls.

### Relevant code areas / 相关代码

- `hermes_cli/web_server.py` — `_lifespan`, `_warm_gateway_module`
- `tui_gateway/ws.py` — `handle_ws` sending `gateway.ready`
- Desktop Electron spawn setting `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`

---

## Local mitigations tried (partial) / 本地缓解（已试，不完全稳定）

These improve reliability but do **not** fully eliminate the race on Windows:

- Await module warm-up **before** accepting WS connections
- Send `gateway.ready` early with an empty/minimal skin; defer skin / MCP work
- Under Desktop (`HERMES_DESKTOP=1`), delay cron / reaper / selftest by ~45s
- Precompile / pre-import hot paths; suggest Defender exclusion for `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`

Upstream needs a durable fix (not just local patches).

---

## Suggested fix / 建议修复

Any of the following (preferably combined):

1. **Startup gate / warm-before-ready**  
   Do not mark the gateway as ready (or do not accept WS / do not send `gateway.ready` until warm-up completes). On Windows (or when `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`), enforce warm-before-ready.

2. **Longer client WS ready timeout on Desktop**  
   Increase renderer wait for `gateway.ready` to cover 30–60s cold-start stalls under Defender.

3. **Minimal ready frame first**  
   Always send a lightweight `gateway.ready` ASAP after accept; load skin / MCP / plugins asynchronously afterward so send cannot fail due to long sync work on the event loop.

4. **Defer non-critical Desktop background work**  
   Cron ticker, reaper, selftest, heavy MCP discovery — schedule after first successful ready (or after a settle delay).

5. **Docs**  
   Document recommending Windows Defender exclusion for `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` for Desktop users.

---

## Impact / 影响

- Severity: **High for Windows Desktop users** — product appears broken (“won't open”) even though the process is running.
- Especially bad on cold start with antivirus real-time scanning.
- Linux/macOS may be less affected; Windows + Defender is the sharp edge.

---

## Additional notes / 补充

- No secrets or personal tokens included; paths use `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`.
- Happy to test a PR / nightly build on Windows 26100 with the unpacked Desktop binary.
- Related search terms for triage: `ready_send_failed`, `event loop stalled`, `GIL pressure`, `gateway.ready`, `HERMES_DESKTOP`.

### Bug Description

After updating to the latest image versions, the nousresearch/hermes-agent container experiences an extreme startup delay (taking several minutes or hanging completely) when a Windows host directory bind mount (-v C:\Users\...:/opt/data) is utilized. This behavior did not occur in older versions.

The delay happens because the initialization script under the new s6-overlay supervision layout appears to perform heavy recursive operations (such as automatic configuration validation, schema patching, or file permission normalization) directly across the mapped persistent data volume. On Windows systems using Docker Desktop (NTFS to Linux translation via gRPC-FUSE/VirtioFS), recursive I/O metadata updates over bind mounts trigger catastrophic performance throttling.

### Steps to Reproduce

1: Run the following command in Windows PowerShell to initialize the container with a local host folder:powershelldocker run -d `
  --name hermes `
  --restart unless-stopped `
  -v C:\Users\asus\.hermes:/opt/data `

  -e HERMES_DASHBOARD=1 `

The entrypoint should optimize initialization workflows when a translation-heavy host file system is detected. It should skip aggressive file-by-file scans on startup or allow an explicit configuration variable to bypass the recursive check if files already exist.

items.title: [Bug]: Successful in-place compression exhausts the shared per-turn attempt budget in long tool loops

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

A long tool-calling turn can become permanently unable to compress even when every earlier compression was successful, materially reduced context, and was followed by successful model calls.

The pre-API, post-tool, 413, and context-overflow paths share one `compression_attempts` counter for the entire turn. Successful maintenance compactions consume the same budget as failed/no-progress retries, and ordinary successful API calls do not reopen the budget. Once the default budget of three is consumed, later context growth within the same turn cannot be compacted.

This is not the rough-token underestimation failure in #62605 and not the first-retry progress-gate issue in #59587. In this report all three compactions made substantial progress.

## Observed timeline (sanitized)

Configuration:

```yaml
agent:
  max_turns: 9000  # intentionally permits a long autonomous tool turn
compression:
  enabled: true
  in_place: true
  max_attempts: 3
```

One Desktop turn performed hundreds of legitimate API/tool iterations. Three proactive in-place compactions committed successfully:

```text
attempt 1/3: ~207,676 rough tokens -> 104,354 actual input on the next successful API call
attempt 2/3: ~205,402 rough tokens -> 110,616 actual input on the next successful API call
attempt 3/3: ~209,793 rough tokens -> 132,596 actual input on the next successful API call
```

Each compaction emitted `split_status="in_place_committed"`. The agent then continued legitimate tool work, so context grew again. At API call 278 the provider reported an actual input of 371,176 tokens and rejected the request. The overflow handler incremented the shared counter beyond the cap and returned:

```text
Context length exceeded: max compression attempts (3) reached. Cannot compress further.
```

A later async completion opened a fresh turn, which reset the counter. In-place compression immediately worked again and successful API inputs fell to approximately 135k-160k. That isolates the failure to the per-turn budget rather than the compressor, provider, or persisted session.

## Expected behavior

A bounded anti-thrash guard should stop repeated failed or no-progress compression attempts.

However, a materially effective compression followed by a successful model call should not permanently consume the failure/retry budget for the rest of a long turn. If later tool output regrows the context, maintenance compression should be available again.

## Actual behavior

The counter is a total-compressions-per-turn cap. Three successful maintenance compactions exhaust it exactly as three failed retries would.

Current regression coverage explicitly enforces this invariant in `tests/run_agent/test_post_tool_compression_attempt_cap.py`:

```text
pre-API and post-tool compactions must share one per-turn attempt budget
```

That protects against compacting after every tool response, but it also strands legitimate long turns after three effective maintenance cycles.

## Steps to reproduce

A deterministic behavioral test can extend the existing post-tool cap test:

1. Run one turn with a long sequence of successful tool calls.
2. Make context pressure cross the threshold four separate times.
3. For each of the first three crossings, have `_compress_context()` materially reduce tokens/messages and let the next API request succeed.
4. Regrow context with additional tool output after each success.
5. On the fourth crossing, return a provider context-overflow error.
6. Observe that no fourth compression can run because the three successful compactions consumed the shared cap.

The test should distinguish this from a compressor that remains under constant pressure without making progress.

## Root cause

`compression_attempts` is initialized once per turn and incremented at proactive, post-tool, 413, and context-overflow sites. It is reset for a fresh turn and some provider/fallback transitions, but not after an effective compaction followed by a successful model call.

The same behavior is present on current `main` at `ef60509a26d07b40c4f512f864c8242a5bce4076`.

## Suggested fix direction

Preserve the safety invariant, but separate:

1. **Consecutive failed/no-progress attempts** — hard-capped (default 3).
2. **Successful maintenance compactions** — allowed again after material progress and a successful model call.

One safe shape would be:

- record pre/post token or message pressure for a compaction;
- only classify it as progress when context decreases materially;
- reset the failure streak only after the compressed request reaches a successful model response;
- retain an absolute cap for consecutive no-progress/provider-overflow retries;
- do not reset immediately before an API call, which could reintroduce an in-loop compaction spin.

Suggested regression coverage:

- four or more effective maintenance compactions can sustain one long tool turn;
- a no-progress compressor still stops after the configured cap;
- pre-API and post-tool sites share the failure streak without sharing a lifetime success quota;
- 413/context-overflow retries remain bounded;
- a successful compression that does not materially reduce pressure does not reset the streak.

## Environment

```text
Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
Installed commit: eb52760564dbba2e5971fa54bd67384e281cd3b8
Current main inspected: ef60509a26d07b40c4f512f864c8242a5bce4076
Client: Hermes Desktop
OS: Ubuntu 24.04
Python: 3.11.15
Compression mode: in_place
```

Raw transcripts and debug bundles are omitted because they contain private tool output. All identifiers, paths, project names, provider details, and message content have been removed; the numeric compression/API telemetry above is retained.

items.title: [Bug] MoA preset fails in cron jobs with 'Authorization: Bearer None' — 'moa://local' endpoint unreachable in isolated cron process

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

MoA (Mixture-of-Agents) presets work correctly in interactive/TUI sessions but **always fail in cron job execution**. Every run produces:

```
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): APIConnectionError
   🔌 Provider: moa  Model: (any MoA preset)
   🌐 Endpoint: moa://local
   📝 Error: Connection error.
```

The request debug dump confirms the root cause:

```json
{
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "moa://local/chat/completions",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer None",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  }
}
```

The `Authorization: Bearer None` header indicates the MoA internal endpoint cannot obtain the required auth token in the isolated cron process environment.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure any MoA preset with reference models and an aggregator in `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   moa:
     presets:
       my-preset:
         enabled: true
         reference_models:
           - provider: deepseek
             model: deepseek-v4-flash
           - provider: some-other-provider
             model: some-model
         aggregator:
           provider: deepseek
           model: deepseek-v4-pro
   ```
2. Create a cron job using this MoA preset:
   ```
   cronjob(action="create", schedule="0 10 * * *", model={"provider":"moa","model":"my-preset"}, ...)
   ```
3. Wait for the cron job to run, or trigger it manually with `cronjob(action="run")`.
4. Observe the job fails with `APIConnectionError` on `moa://local`.

## Expected Behavior

MoA presets should work identically in cron jobs and interactive sessions. The cron process should inherit or be able to initialize the same auth context that MoA needs internally.

## Actual Behavior

Every cron run fails with `Connection error` after 3 retries. The underlying `moa://local` endpoint cannot authenticate itself (`Bearer None`). This is consistent across multiple attempts with no variation — regardless of which MoA preset is used.

## Environment

- Hermes version: latest (v0.19.0+)
- Provider: moa (local aggregation)
- Cron delivery: origin,local
- Profile: single-profile (non-multiplexed) deployment
- OS: Linux (Debian, Docker container)

## Related Issues

- #65773 — Cron scheduler installs profile secret scope unconditionally, breaks env-injected credentials on single-profile deployments
- #55539 — Worker spawn produces Authorization: Bearer None on first LLM call (same auth token symptom)
- #71244 — MoA selection inconsistencies (related internal routing)
- #69734 — Cron agent run hangs on 2nd consecutive streaming inference call (cron env general issues)

## Workaround

Using a single model (e.g. `deepseek:deepseek-chat`) in the cron job instead of the MoA preset works correctly. The issue is specific to MoA's internal `moa://local` endpoint authentication in isolated cron processes.

## Possible Root Cause

`moa://local` is an internal Hermes endpoint that routes through the MoA aggregation pipeline. In interactive/TUI sessions, the auth context is established during session initialization. In cron jobs, the process is spawned in isolation without this context, causing the MoA handler to produce `Authorization: Bearer None` when proxying requests to reference models.

items.title: Startup takes minutes — `_find_installed_skill_dir_by_name` runs a full `SKILLS_DIR.rglob` once per optional skill (regression `72de75c0a` / v2026.7.20)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

Since v2026.7.20, `hermes -p <profile> chat` takes ~4 minutes to start. Blame narrows it to a single commit (`72de75c0a`) that introduced `_find_installed_skill_dir_by_name`, which runs `SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md")` **once per optional skill** during startup provenance backfill — O(N × |SKILLS_DIR|) where it could be O(N + |SKILLS_DIR|).

## Environment
- hermes-agent 0.19.0 (v2026.7.20, HEAD `2078af601`)
- Windows 11, Python 3.11.15
- SKILLS_DIR = `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/skills`: ~73,864 files (includes `node_modules` from node-based skills like `wenyan-mcp`)
- 111 optional skills in the bundled catalog

## Root cause

`_sync_bundled_skills_for_startup` (`hermes_cli/main.py:921`, runs on every non-Termux start) → `sync_skills` → `_backfill_optional_provenance` (`tools/skills_sync.py:462`) iterates the 111 optional skills. For each whose expected dest path doesn't exist, it falls back to:

```python
# tools/skills_sync.py:481
dest = _find_installed_skill_dir_by_name(src.name)
```

and that helper does:

```python
# tools/skills_sync.py:418
for skill_md in SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md"):
    ...
```

Because upstream category reorgs mean dest paths usually don't match a previously-installed copy, the fallback fires for most of the 111 skills → roughly **100 full recursive scans of a 73k-file tree** per startup.

## Evidence

`faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(8, repeat=True)` (injected via `PYTHONPATH` sitecustomize) captured the main thread parked in this exact chain across 5 consecutive 8 s samples:

```
pathlib._iterate_directories / _scandir / stat        (sustained)
  tools/skills_sync.py:418   SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md")
  tools/skills_sync.py:405   _find_installed_skill_dir_by_name
  tools/skills_sync.py:481   _backfill_optional_provenance
  tools/skills_sync.py:897   sync_skills
  hermes_cli/main.py:921     _sync_bundled_skills_for_startup
  hermes_cli/main.py:2574    cmd_chat
```

Single `SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md")` here ≈ 1.9 s warm (worse cold). ~100 fallback calls → minutes of silent startup (no log lines emitted during the scan).

## Regression scope (git blame)

- `_find_installed_skill_dir_by_name` definition (L405), the `rglob` (L418), and the per-skill call site (L481) **all blame to `72de75c0a`** — `feat(curator): surface unmanaged skills and add "curator adopt"` (Teknium, 2026-07-25, v2026.7.20).
- The enclosing `_backfill_optional_provenance` is older (`f040710d04`, v2026.5.16) but previously used path-only lookup and did **not** tree-scan.
- Confirmed: v2026.5.16 starts fast; v2026.7.20 starts in ~4 min.

## Suggested fix

Build the name→dir index **once** instead of rglob per skill:

```python
def _skill_dir_by_name() -> dict[str, Path]:
    if not SKILLS_DIR.exists():
        return {}
    idx: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for skill_md in SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md"):
        if is_excluded_skill_path(skill_md):
            continue
        idx.setdefault(skill_md.parent.name, skill_md.parent)
    return idx
```

Then `_find_installed_skill_dir_by_name(name)` becomes a dict lookup. Optional: prune `node_modules`/`.git` during the single rglob to shrink the traversal.

After this change (or the workaround below) my startup goes from ~4 min to ~21 s.

## Workaround

`HERMES_HOME/.no-bundled-skills` marker file → `sync_skills` returns early (`skills_sync.py:664`). Downside: bundled skills no longer auto-sync on upgrade.

items.title: fix(gateway): NameError on `_history_media_paths` in `already_sent` branch of `_handle_message_with_agent`

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
